## P2 - Netem support check is bypassed on the default Topology-CR deploy path in `Deploy`

**Location:** [labruntime/clabernetes/lifecycle.go:88-106](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/9c4339862aaf88770cd98d951e994c7f5afb87f2/labruntime/clabernetes/lifecycle.go#L88-L106)

**Problem:** In `Deploy`, the `linksDeclareNetem`/`ensureLinkNetemSupport` guard is placed after the early returns for `existingTopology != nil` &#40;`reconcileTopology`&#41; and `!req.NoTopologyCR` &#40;`deployTopology`&#41;, so only the `--no-topology-cr` branch runs it. Neither `deployTopology` &#40;[`labruntime/clabernetes/reconcile.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/9c4339862aaf88770cd98d951e994c7f5afb87f2/labruntime/clabernetes/reconcile.go#L1-L1) L404-L497&#41; nor `reconcileTopology` &#40;L534-L593&#41; performs the check.

**Trigger:** Run `containerlab -r c9s deploy -t lab.clab.yml` &#40;the default path that creates a Topology CR&#41; with a topology declaring `netem` against a cluster running clabernetes older than 0.12.

**Impact:** An older controller &#40;or Topology CRD pruning&#41; drops the impairment and the lab deploys silently unimpaired, which is exactly the failure mode the PR&#39;s own comments in [`support.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/9c4339862aaf88770cd98d951e994c7f5afb87f2/labruntime/clabernetes/support.go#L1-L1) &#40;`requiredClabernetesNetem`&#41; and the new docs in [`docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/9c4339862aaf88770cd98d951e994c7f5afb87f2/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md#L1-L1) promise to prevent. On a Topology-owned lab `SetImpairment` rejects changes by design, so the user cannot discover or work around the missing support with `tools netem` either.

**Suggested correction:** Hoist the guard above the two early returns in `Deploy`; `prepareDesiredDeployment` &#40;[`labruntime/clabernetes/plan.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/9c4339862aaf88770cd98d951e994c7f5afb87f2/labruntime/clabernetes/plan.go#L1-L1) L27&#41; always compiles `primitives` on both paths, so `prepared.primitives.links` is available there. Adjust the comment, which currently describes only the `--no-topology-cr` branch, and add a unit test asserting that `Deploy` fails on both paths with a netem-declaring topology and an unsupported cluster.


## P4 - All-zero `tools netem set` on a lab runtime writes `netem: {}` and prints nothing

**Location:** [labruntime/clabernetes/netem.go:204-225](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/9c4339862aaf88770cd98d951e994c7f5afb87f2/labruntime/clabernetes/netem.go#L204-L225)

**Problem:** `netemSetLabRuntime` &#40;[`cmd/tools_netem_labruntime.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/9c4339862aaf88770cd98d951e994c7f5afb87f2/cmd/tools_netem_labruntime.go#L1-L1) L42-L68&#41; always passes a non-nil `&Impairment{}`; with all-zero values `linkNetem` returns an empty map, which the merge patch writes as `netem: {}`. `Impairments` skips endpoints with an empty `netem` &#40;L141&#41;, so the post-set confirmation table prints nothing and `show` reports the interface as unimpaired. Local `tools netem set` with all zeros instead replaces the qdisc with a zero-impairment `netem` qdisc &#40;[`netem/netem.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/9c4339862aaf88770cd98d951e994c7f5afb87f2/netem/netem.go#L1-L1), `ReplaceImpairments`&#41;.

**Trigger:** Run `containerlab -r c9s tools netem set -t lab.clab.yml -n r1 -i eth1` without any impairment flags.

**Impact:** A silent no-op that leaves an empty object in the Link CR, and a cosmetic inconsistency between the local and lab-runtime behavior of the same command.

**Suggested correction:** Treat an all-zero impairment as a `reset` in `netemSetLabRuntime` &#40;pass `nil` for `Impairment`&#41;, or skip the patch when all fields are zero, so `set`, `show`, and `reset` stay consistent.


## Coverage

- Source-only review&#58; tests, linters, and formatters were not executed and no CI results were supplied.
- All 22 changed paths from `manifest.json` were reviewed, including every diff hunk, the deploy-path flow, capability wiring, support checks, tests, docs, `go.mod/go.sum`, and the e2e suite.
- Command gating verified&#58; `checkLabRuntimeCommandSupport` walks parent commands and breaks on the `tools.netem` path; other `tools` subcommands remain rejected, covered by [`cmd/root_test.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/9c4339862aaf88770cd98d951e994c7f5afb87f2/cmd/root_test.go#L1-L1).
- Schema check&#58; [`schemas/clab.schema.json`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/9c4339862aaf88770cd98d951e994c7f5afb87f2/schemas/clab.schema.json#L1-L1) is unchanged and already carries `netem` on links; the new test topology validates against it. The c9s Link CRD schema is external &#40;clabernetes v0.12.0&#41; and is validated at runtime via the `OpenAPI` check with a committed fixture.
- Unverified by execution&#58; whether clabernetes 0.11 prunes or rejects link-level `netem` on Topology admission; the P2 conclusion &#40;silent unimpaired deploy on the default path&#41; holds either way.
- The documented 4 m delay ceiling &#40;32-bit kernel ticks&#41; is not validated client-side; it is an external clabernetes/kernel constraint disclosed in [`docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/9c4339862aaf88770cd98d951e994c7f5afb87f2/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md#L1-L1) that local `netem` shares, recorded here rather than as a finding.
- The generated `docs/cmd/tools/netem/*.md` pages are unchanged, consistent with the unchanged Long help texts of the `netem` commands.

<content>
1: ---
2: description: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Use when writing, reviewing, or refactoring code to avoid overcomplication, make surgical changes, surface assumptions, and define verifiable success criteria.
3: alwaysApply: true
4: ---
5: 
6: # Karpathy behavioral guidelines
7: 
8: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Merge with project-specific instructions as needed.
9: 
10: **Tradeoff:** These guidelines bias toward caution over speed. For trivial tasks, use judgment.
11: 
12: ## 1. Think Before Coding
13: 
14: **Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.**
15: 
16: Before implementing:
17: 
18: - State your assumptions explicitly. If uncertain, ask.
19: - If multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently.
20: - If a simpler approach exists, say so. Push back when warranted.
21: - If something is unclear, stop. Name what's confusing. Ask.
22: 
23: ## 2. Simplicity First
24: 
25: **Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.**
26: 
27: - No features beyond what was asked.
28: - No abstractions for single-use code.
29: - No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested.
30: - No error handling for impossible scenarios.
31: - If you write 200 lines and it could be 50, rewrite it.
32: 
33: Ask yourself: "Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated?" If yes, simplify.
34: 
35: ## 3. Surgical Changes
36: 
37: **Touch only what you must. Clean up only your own mess.**
38: 
39: When editing existing code:
40: 
41: - Don't "improve" adjacent code, comments, or formatting.
42: - Don't refactor things that aren't broken.
43: - Match existing style, even if you'd do it differently.
44: - If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it - don't delete it.
45: 
46: When your changes create orphans:
47: 
48: - Remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR changes made unused.
49: - Don't remove pre-existing dead code unless asked.
50: 
51: The test: Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.
52: 
53: ## 4. Goal-Driven Execution
54: 
55: **Define success criteria. Loop until verified.**
56: 
57: Transform tasks into verifiable goals:
58: 
59: - "Add validation" → "Write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass"
60: - "Fix the bug" → "Write a test that reproduces it, then make it pass"
61: - "Refactor X" → "Ensure tests pass before and after"
62: 
63: For multi-step tasks, state a brief plan:
64: 
65: ```
66: 1. [Step] → verify: [check]
67: 2. [Step] → verify: [check]
68: 3. [Step] → verify: [check]
69: ```
70: 
71: Strong success criteria let you loop independently. Weak criteria ("make it work") require constant clarification.
72: 
73: ---
74: 
75: **These guidelines are working if:** fewer unnecessary changes in diffs, fewer rewrites due to overcomplication, and clarifying questions come before implementation rather than after mistakes.

(End of file - total 75 lines)
</content>

1: ---
2: description: Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode. Always pick the simplest solution that works.
3: globs:
4: alwaysApply: true
5: ---
6: 
7: # Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode
8: 
9: You are a lazy senior developer. Lazy means efficient, not careless. The best code is the code never written.
10: 
11: Before writing any code, stop at the first rung that holds:
12: 
13: 1. Does this need to be built at all? (YAGNI)
14: 2. Does it already exist in this codebase? Reuse the helper, util, or pattern that's already here, don't re-write it.
15: 3. Does the standard library already do this? Use it.
16: 4. Does a native platform feature cover it? Use it.
17: 5. Does an already-installed dependency solve it? Use it.
18: 6. Can this be one line? Make it one line.
19: 7. Only then: write the minimum code that works.
20: 
21: The ladder runs after you understand the problem, not instead of it: read the task and the code it touches, trace the real flow end to end, then climb.
22: 
23: Bug fix = root cause, not symptom: a report names a symptom. Grep every caller of the function you touch and fix the shared function once — one guard there is a smaller diff than one per caller, and patching only the path the ticket names leaves a sibling caller still broken.
24: 
25: Rules:
26: 
27: - No abstractions that weren't explicitly requested.
28: - No new dependency if it can be avoided.
29: - No boilerplate nobody asked for.
30: - Deletion over addition. Boring over clever. Fewest files possible.
31: - Shortest working diff wins, but only once you understand the problem. The smallest change in the wrong place isn't lazy, it's a second bug.
32: - Question complex requests: "Do you actually need X, or does Y cover it?"
33: - Pick the edge-case-correct option when two stdlib approaches are the same size, lazy means less code, not the flimsier algorithm.
34: - Mark deliberate simplifications that cut a real corner with a known ceiling (global lock, O(n²) scan, naive heuristic) with a `ponytail:` comment naming the ceiling and upgrade path.
35: 
36: Not lazy about: understanding the problem (read it fully and trace the real flow before picking a rung, a small diff you don't understand is just laziness dressed up as efficiency), input validation at trust boundaries, error handling that prevents data loss, security, accessibility, the calibration real hardware needs (the platform is never the spec ideal, a clock drifts, a sensor reads off), anything explicitly requested. Lazy code without its check is unfinished: non-trivial logic leaves ONE runnable check behind, the smallest thing that fails if the logic breaks (an assert-based demo/self-check or one small test file; no frameworks, no fixtures). Trivial one-liners need no test.

(End of file - total 36 lines)
</content>

216: +	return nil
217: +}
218: +
219: +func netemShowLabRuntime(ctx context.Context, o *Options) error {
220: +	c, err := netemLab(o)
221: +	if err != nil {
222: +		return err
223: +	}
224: +
225: +	var requested []string
226: +	if o.ToolsNetem.ContainerName != "" {
227: +		requested = []string{o.ToolsNetem.ContainerName}
228: +	}
229: +
230: +	nodes, err := c.LinkImpairments(ctx, requested)
231: +	if err != nil {
232: +		return err
233: +	}
234: +
235: +	if o.ToolsNetem.Format == clabconstants.FormatJSON {
236: +		impairments := make(map[string][]clabtypes.ImpairmentData, len(nodes))
237: +		for _, node := range nodes {
238: +			impairments[node.Node] = node.Impairments
239: +		}
240: +
241: +		jsonData, err := json.MarshalIndent(impairments, "", "  ")
242: +		if err != nil {
243: +			return fmt.Errorf("error marshaling JSON: %v", err)
244: +		}
245: +
246: +		fmt.Println(string(jsonData))
247: +
248: +		return nil
249: +	}
250: +
251: +	for _, node := range nodes {
252: +		if len(requested) == 0 {
253: +			fmt.Printf("\n=== Node: %s ===\n", node.Node)
254: +		}
255: +
256: +		rows := make([]tableWriter.Row, 0, len(node.Impairments))
257: +		for _, impairment := range node.Impairments {
258: +			rows = append(rows, impairmentTableRow(impairment))
259: +		}
260: +
261: +		printImpairments(rows)
262: +	}
263: +
264: +	return nil
265: +}
266: +
267: +func netemResetLabRuntime(ctx context.Context, o *Options) error {
268: +	c, err := netemLab(o)
269: +	if err != nil {
270: +		return err
271: +	}
272: +
273: +	err = c.SetLinkImpairment(ctx, clablabruntime.ImpairmentRequest{
274: +		Node:      o.ToolsNetem.ContainerName,
275: +		Interface: o.ToolsNetem.Interface,
276: +	})
277: +	if err != nil {
278: +		return err
279: +	}
280: +
281: +	fmt.Printf("Reset impairments on node %q, interface %q\n",
282: +		o.ToolsNetem.ContainerName, o.ToolsNetem.Interface)
283: +
284: +	return nil
285: +}
286: +
287: +// impairmentTableRow formats an impairment like the table tools netem show prints for local
288: +// labs.
289: +func impairmentTableRow(impairment clabtypes.ImpairmentData) tableWriter.Row {
290: +	return tableWriter.Row{
291: +		impairment.Interface,
292: +		impairment.Delay,
293: +		impairment.Jitter,
294: +		strconv.FormatFloat(impairment.PacketLoss, 'f', 2, 64) + "%",
295: +		strconv.Itoa(impairment.Rate),
296: +		strconv.FormatFloat(impairment.Corruption, 'f', 2, 64) + "%",
297: +	}
298: +}

460: +func (c *CLab) SetLinkImpairment(
461: +	ctx context.Context,
462: +	req clablabruntime.ImpairmentRequest,
463: +) error {
464: +	impairer, err := c.linkImpairer()
465: +	if err != nil {
466: +		return err
467: +	}
468: +
469: +	if req.Name == "" {

471: +	}
472: +	if req.Identity.IsZero() {
473: +		req.Identity = c.labRuntimeIdentity
474: +	}
475: +
476: +	return impairer.SetImpairment(ctx, req)
477: +}
478: +
479: +// LinkImpairments lists the impaired lab link interfaces of the given nodes, or of every node,
480: +// through the lab runtime.
481: +func (c *CLab) LinkImpairments(
482: +	ctx context.Context,
483: +	nodes []string,
484: +) ([]clablabruntime.NodeImpairments, error) {
485: +	impairer, err := c.linkImpairer()
486: +	if err != nil {
487: +		return nil, err
488: +	}
489: +
490: +	return impairer.Impairments(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{
491: +		Name:     c.Config.Name,

493: +		Identity: c.labRuntimeIdentity,
494: +	})
495: +}

503: +		return nil, err
504: +	}

508: diff --git a/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md b/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md
509: index 3a959ea..bd1e07e 100644
510: --- a/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md
511: +++ b/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md
512: @@ -701,10 +701,45 @@ Capturing needs `get` and `create` on `pods/exec` in the lab namespace, which
513:  `clabernetes-lab-editor` grants. `inspect interfaces -r c9s` lists the same
514:  interfaces, with the MAC address, index, MTU and operational state read from
515:  sysfs in the device container (type `veth`, which is how `clabwire` realizes
516:  lab links).
517:  
518: +## Link impairments
519: +
520: +[Impairments in the topology](../impairments.md#declarative-definition)
521: +become the `netem` of the matching endpoint of each c9s Link. On a link between
522: +Pods, the peer Pod's `clabwire` sidecar programs the impairment on its own
523: +sidecar leg, where it receives the endpoint's packets. On same-Pod and host
524: +links, it programs the endpoint's interface instead. It also sets the impairment
525: +again when the interface is recreated, so it survives node restarts without
526: +containerlab.
527: +
528: +In a lab deployed with `--no-topology-cr`, [`tools netem`](../../cmd/tools/netem/set.md)
529: +changes the Link instead of a local network namespace, and `clabwire` applies
530: +the change live, without restarting the node. The change reaches `clabwire`
531: +through a ConfigMap the kubelet syncs into its pod, which can take a minute. It needs `--topo` or `--name`,
532: +and no root privileges:
533: +
534: +```bash
535: +containerlab -r c9s tools netem set -t clos.clab.yml -n srl1 -i e1-1 --delay 50ms --loss 1
536: +containerlab -r c9s tools netem show -t clos.clab.yml
537: +containerlab -r c9s tools netem reset -t clos.clab.yml -n srl1 -i e1-1
538: +```
539: +
540: +`show` lists the impairments the Links declare. A later `deploy` replaces each
541: +Link with the one the topology compiles to, which restores the topology's
542: +impairments, like `start` and `apply` do for local labs. A lab owned by a
543: +Topology resource (the default) rejects `set` and `reset`: the clabernetes
544: +controller renders its Links and reverts any direct change, so its impairments
545: +come from the topology.
546: +
547: +Link impairments need a clabernetes release whose Link has an endpoint
548: +`netem`. containerlab checks the published Link schema the first time a lab
549: +uses them, because an older release would drop the field and deploy the lab
550: +unimpaired. clabernetes programs the delay in 32-bit kernel ticks, so it
551: +accepts delays up to `4m`.
552: +
553:  ## Start, stop, and restart
554:  
555:  Node lifecycle commands ask the clabernetes controllers for a run state; they
556:  never touch Deployments or Pods.
557:

563:  - `inspect interfaces` lists only the lab link interfaces (those `capture`

565: -  operations do not have the same local namespace access they have with Docker
566: -  labs.

571:    container, so it needs Docker or Podman on the outer host.

573: -  rejected with an error when the `c9s` runtime is selected.
574: +  rejected with an error when the `c9s` runtime is selected, except
575: +  [`tools netem`](#link-impairments), which changes the lab's Links.

On veth-stitch links, which brief links of SR-SIM nodes use, containerlab sets them on the stitch, like `tools netem set` does, since impairments on the interfaces of SR-SIM nodes have no effect. On SR-SIM endpoints of extended `veth` links they have no effect either, and containerlab warns about it.
592: -
593: -> [clabernetes](clabernetes/runtime.md) lab runtime doesn't support declarative impairments yet, so deploying a topology with impairments there fails, as do starting or restarting its nodes.
594: +Impairments are supported on the node endpoints of [veth](topo-def-file.md#veth) and [veth-stitch](topo-def-file.md#veth-stitch) links; other link types and `host` or `mgmt-net` endpoints reject them. On veth-stitch links, which brief links of SR-SIM nodes use, containerlab sets them on the stitch, like `tools netem set` does, since impairments on the interfaces of SR-SIM nodes have no effect. On SR-SIM endpoints of extended `veth` links they have no effect either, and containerlab warns about it. With the [clabernetes runtime](clabernetes/runtime.md#link-impairments), the impairments become part of the lab's Links, and `tools netem` changes them there.
595:  
596:  Containerlab sets them again when a node is started or restarted, since a node's interfaces lose their impairments when it is stopped, and whenever the lab is deployed again. `tools netem` can still change them while the lab runs, until containerlab sets the topology's impairments again. Removing an impairment from the topology, or setting all of its values to zero, doesn't remove it from a running lab; use `tools netem reset` for that.

784: @@ -98,10 +98,13 @@ type Runtime struct {

935: +// SetImpairment sets the netem impairment of one lab link interface on the endpoint of its c9s
936: +// Link, or removes it when the request carries none. The connectivity sidecar of the node's pod
937: +// applies the change live; a later deploy restores the impairments the topology declares. A lab
938: +// owned by a Topology resource is rejected: its controller renders the Links and reverts any
939: +// direct change, so its impairments come from the topology.
940: +func (r *Runtime) SetImpairment(
941: +	ctx context.Context,
942: +	req clablabruntime.ImpairmentRequest,
943: +) error {
944: +	r, err := r.connect(ctx, req.Identity)
945: +	if err != nil {
946: +		return err
947: +	}
948: +
949: +	if err = r.ensureLinkNetemSupport(ctx); err != nil {
950: +		return err
951: +	}
952: +
953: +	locations, err := r.LocateNode(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{
954: +		Name: req.Name, Namespace: req.Namespace, Nodes: []string{req.Node},
955: +		Identity: req.Identity,
956: +	})
957: +	if err != nil {
958: +		return err
959: +	}
960: +	location := locations[0]
961: +
962: +	_, err = r.client.Resource(topologyGVR).Namespace(location.Namespace).
963: +		Get(ctx, req.Name, metav1.GetOptions{})
964: +	switch {
965: +	case err == nil:
966: +		return fmt.Errorf("c9s lab %s/%s is owned by a Topology resource, whose controller "+
967: +			"reverts changes to its links; declare the impairment in the topology and deploy "+
968: +			"again, or deploy the lab with --no-topology-cr", location.Namespace, req.Name)
969: +	case !apierrors.IsNotFound(err):
970: +		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get clabernetes topology %s/%s: %w",
971: +			location.Namespace, req.Name, err)
972: +	}
973: +
974: +	links, err := r.primitiveResourcesForTopology(ctx, linkGVR, req.Name, location.Namespace)
975: +	if err != nil {
976: +		return err
977: +	}
978: +
979: +	link, endpoint, ok := linkEndpoint(links.Items, location.NodeName, req.Interface)
980: +	if !ok {
981: +		return fmt.Errorf("interface %q of node %q is not on a link of c9s lab %s/%s",
982: +			req.Interface, req.Node, location.Namespace, req.Name)
983: +	}
984: +
985: +	// a merge patch with a null netem removes it
986: +	var netem any
987: +	if req.Impairment != nil {
988: +		netem = linkNetem(req.Impairment)
989: +	}
990: +
991: +	patch, err := json.Marshal(map[string]any{
992: +		"spec": map[string]any{endpoint: map[string]any{"netem": netem}},
993: +	})
994: +	if err != nil {
995: +		return err
996: +	}
997: +
998: +	_, err = r.client.Resource(linkGVR).Namespace(location.Namespace).Patch(
999: +		ctx, link.GetName(), types.MergePatchType, patch, metav1.PatchOptions{},
1000: +	)
1001: +	if err != nil {
1002: +		return fmt.Errorf("failed to set the impairment of c9s link %s/%s: %w",
1003: +			location.Namespace, link.GetName(), err)
1004: +	}
1005: +
1006: +	return nil
1007: +}

1009: +// Impairments lists the impaired link interfaces of the requested nodes, or of every node, as
1010: +// their c9s Links declare them.
1011: +func (r *Runtime) Impairments(
1012: +	ctx context.Context,
1013: +	req clablabruntime.NodeRequest,
1014: +) ([]clablabruntime.NodeImpairments, error) {
1015: +	r, err := r.connect(ctx, req.Identity)
1016: +	if err != nil {
1017: +		return nil, err
1018: +	}
1019: +
1020: +	locations, err := r.LocateNode(ctx, req)
1021: +	if err != nil || len(locations) == 0 {
1022: +		return nil, err
1023: +	}
1024: +
1025: +	names, err := r.nodeDisplayNames(ctx, req.Name, locations)
1026: +	if err != nil {
1027: +		return nil, err
1028: +	}
1029: +
1030: +	links, err := r.client.Resource(linkGVR).Namespace(locations[0].Namespace).List(
1031: +		ctx,
1032: +		metav1.ListOptions{LabelSelector: labels.Set{labelTopologyOwner: req.Name}.String()},
1033: +	)
1034: +	if err != nil {
1035: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to list c9s links for lab %s/%s: %w",
1036: +			locations[0].Namespace, req.Name, err)
1037: +	}
1038: +
1039: +	impairments := map[string][]clabtypes.ImpairmentData{}
1040: +	for _, location := range locations {
1041: +		impairments[location.NodeName] = nil
1042: +	}
1043: +
1044: +	for idx := range links.Items {
1045: +		for _, endpoint := range linkEndpointFields {
1046: +			node, _, _ := unstructured.NestedString(links.Items[idx].Object,
1047: +				"spec", endpoint, "nodeName")
1048: +			iface, _, _ := unstructured.NestedString(links.Items[idx].Object,
1049: +				"spec", endpoint, "interfaceName")
1050: +			netem, found, _ := unstructured.NestedMap(links.Items[idx].Object,
1051: +				"spec", endpoint, "netem")
1052: +
1053: +			if _, requested := impairments[node]; !requested || !found || len(netem) == 0 {
1054: +				continue
1055: +			}
1056: +
1057: +			impairments[node] = append(impairments[node], impairmentData(iface, netem))
1058: +		}
1059: +	}
1060: +
1061: +	result := make([]clablabruntime.NodeImpairments, 0, len(locations))
1062: +	for _, location := range locations {
1063: +		nodeImpairments := impairments[location.NodeName]
1064: +		sort.Slice(nodeImpairments, func(i, j int) bool {
1065: +			return nodeImpairments[i].Interface < nodeImpairments[j].Interface
1066: +		})
1067: +
1068: +		result = append(result, clablabruntime.NodeImpairments{
1069: +			Node:        names.display(location.NodeName),
1070: +			Impairments: nodeImpairments,
1071: +		})
1072: +	}
1073: +
1074: +	sort.Slice(result, func(i, j int) bool { return result[i].Node < result[j].Node })
1075: +
1076: +	return result, nil
1077: +}

1079: +// linksDeclareNetem reports whether any of the Links impairs one of its endpoints.
1080: +func linksDeclareNetem(links []*unstructured.Unstructured) bool {
1081: +	for _, link := range links {
1082: +		for _, endpoint := range linkEndpointFields {
1083: +			if _, found, _ := unstructured.NestedFieldNoCopy(link.Object,
1084: +				"spec", endpoint, "netem"); found {
1085: +				return true
1086: +			}
1087: +		}
1088: +	}
1089: +
1090: +	return false
1091: +}
1092: +
1093: +// linkEndpoint finds the c9s Link with an endpoint on the node's interface and returns it with
1094: +// the spec field of that endpoint.
1095: +func linkEndpoint(
1096: +	links []unstructured.Unstructured,
1097: +	node,
1098: +	iface string,
1099: +) (*unstructured.Unstructured, string, bool) {
1100: +	for idx := range links {
1101: +		for _, endpoint := range linkEndpointFields {
1102: +			endpointNode, _, _ := unstructured.NestedString(links[idx].Object,
1103: +				"spec", endpoint, "nodeName")
1104: +			endpointIface, _, _ := unstructured.NestedString(links[idx].Object,
1105: +				"spec", endpoint, "interfaceName")
1106: +
1107: +			if endpointNode == node && endpointIface == iface {
1108: +				return &links[idx], endpoint, true
1109: +			}
1110: +		}
1111: +	}
1112: +
1113: +	return nil, "", false
1114: +}
1115: +
1116: +// linkNetem renders an impairment in the c9s Link vocabulary, which is containerlab's.
1117: +func linkNetem(impairment *clablabruntime.Impairment) map[string]any {
1118: +	netem := map[string]any{}
1119: +
1120: +	if impairment.Delay != 0 {
1121: +		netem["delay"] = impairment.Delay.String()
1122: +	}
1123: +	if impairment.Jitter != 0 {
1124: +		netem["jitter"] = impairment.Jitter.String()
1125: +	}
1126: +	if impairment.Loss != 0 {
1127: +		netem["loss"] = impairment.Loss
1128: +	}
1129: +	if impairment.Rate != 0 {
1130: +		netem["rate"] = impairment.Rate
1131: +	}
1132: +	if impairment.Corruption != 0 {
1133: +		netem["corruption"] = impairment.Corruption
1134: +	}
1135: +
1136: +	return netem
1137: +}
1138: +
1139: +// impairmentData converts a c9s Link endpoint netem into the shape tools netem show reports for
1140: +// local labs.
1141: +func impairmentData(iface string, netem map[string]any) clabtypes.ImpairmentData {
1142: +	data := clabtypes.ImpairmentData{Interface: iface}
1143: +
1144: +	if delay, ok := netem["delay"].(string); ok {
1145: +		data.Delay = normalizedDuration(delay)
1146: +	}
1147: +	if jitter, ok := netem["jitter"].(string); ok {
1148: +		data.Jitter = normalizedDuration(jitter)
1149: +	}
1150: +
1151: +	data.PacketLoss = roundedPercent(netem["loss"])
1152: +	data.Corruption = roundedPercent(netem["corruption"])
1153: +
1154: +	switch rate := netem["rate"].(type) {
1155: +	case int64:
1156: +		data.Rate = int(rate)
1157: +	case float64:
1158: +		data.Rate = int(rate)
1159: +	}
1160: +
1161: +	return data
1162: +}
1163: +
1164: +func normalizedDuration(value string) string {
1165: +	duration, err := time.ParseDuration(value)
1166: +	if err != nil {
1167: +		return value
1168: +	}
1169: +
1170: +	return duration.String()
1171: +}
1172: +
1173: +// roundedPercent rounds a percentage to 2 decimal places, like tools netem show.
1174: +func roundedPercent(value any) float64 {
1175: +	var percent float64
1176: +
1177: +	switch typed := value.(type) {
1178: +	case int64:
1179: +		percent = float64(typed)
1180: +	case float64:
1181: +		percent = typed
1182: +	}
1183: +
1184: +	return math.Round(percent*100) / 100 //nolint:mnd
1185: +}

Capturing needs `get` and `create` on `pods/exec` in the lab namespace, which\n513:  `clabernetes-lab-editor` grants. `inspect interfaces -r c9s` lists the same\n514:  interfaces, with the MAC address, index, MTU and operational state read from\n515:  sysfs in the device container (type `veth`, which is how `clabwire` realizes\n516:  lab links).\n517:  \n518: +## Link impairments\n519: +\n520: +[Impairments in the topology](../impairments.md#declarative-definition)\n521: +become the `netem` of the matching endpoint of each c9s Link. On a link between\n522: +Pods, the peer Pod's `clabwire` sidecar programs the impairment on its own\n523: +sidecar leg, where it receives the endpoint's packets. On same-Pod and host\n524: +links, it programs the endpoint's interface instead. It also sets the impairment\n525: +again when the interface is recreated, so it survives node restarts without\n526: +containerlab.\n527: +\n528: +In a lab deployed with `--no-topology-cr`, [`tools netem`](../../cmd/tools/netem/set.md)\n529: +changes the Link instead of a local network namespace, and `clabwire` applies\n530: +the change live, without restarting the node. The change reaches `clabwire`\n531: +through a ConfigMap the kubelet syncs into its pod, which can take a minute. It needs `--topo` or `--name`,\n532: +and no root privileges:\n533: +\n534: +```bash\n535: +containerlab -r c9s tools netem set -t clos.clab.yml -n srl1 -i e1-1 --delay 50ms --loss 1\n536: +containerlab -r c9s tools netem show -t clos.clab.yml\n537: +containerlab -r c9s tools netem reset -t clos.clab.yml -n srl1 -i e1-1\n538: +```\n539: +\n540: +`show` lists the impairments the Links declare. A later `deploy` replaces each\n541: +Link with the one the topology compiles to, which restores the topology's\n542: +impairments, like `start` and `apply` do for local labs. A lab owned by a\n543: +Topology resource (the default) rejects `set` and `reset`: the clabernetes\n544: +controller renders its Links and reverts any direct change, so its impairments\n545: +come from the topology.\n546: +\n547: +Link impairments need a clabernetes release whose Link has an endpoint\n548: +`netem`. containerlab checks the published Link schema the first time a lab\n549: +uses them, because an older release would drop the field and deploy the lab\n550: +unimpaired. clabernetes programs the delay in 32-bit kernel ticks, so it\n551: +accepts delays up to `4m`.\n552: +\n553:  ## Start, stop, and restart\n554:  \n555:  Node lifecycle commands ask the clabernetes controllers for a run state; they\n556:  never touch Deployments or Pods.\n557:  \n558: @@ -1413,19 +1448,18 @@ Known command differences:\n559:  - Destroy flags `--graceful` and `--keep-mgmt-net` are rejected. `--cleanup`\n560:    also deletes the lab's persistent claims (saved device state) and removes\n561:    the local lab directory; a plain destroy keeps the claims.\n562:  - Local Docker commands on the outer host are not authoritative for c9s labs.\n563:  - `inspect interfaces` lists only the lab link interfaces (those `capture`\n564: -  accepts), not the management or pod interfaces. topology](../impairments.md#declarative-definition)\n+become the `netem` of the matching endpoint of each c9s Link. On a link between\n+Pods, the peer Pod's `clabwire` sidecar programs the impairment on its own\n+sidecar leg, where it receives the endpoint's packets. On same-Pod and host\n+links, it programs the endpoint's interface instead. It also sets the impairment\n+again when the interface is recreated, so it survives node restarts without\n+containerlab.\n+\n+In a lab deployed with `--no-topology-cr`, [`tools netem`](../../cmd/tools/netem/set.md)\n+changes the Link instead of a local network namespace, and `clabwire` applies\n+the change live, without restarting the node. The change reaches `clabwire`\n+through a ConfigMap the kubelet syncs into its pod, which can take a minute. It needs `--topo` or `--name`,\n+and no root privileges:\n+\n+```bash\n+containerlab -r c9s tools netem set -t clos.clab.yml -n srl1 -i e1-1 --delay 50ms --loss 1\n+containerlab -r c9s tools netem show -t clos.clab.yml\n+containerlab -r c9s tools netem reset -t clos.clab.yml -n srl1 -i e1-1\n+```\n+\n+`show` lists the impairments the Links declare. A later `deploy` replaces each\n+Link with the one the topology compiles to, which restores the topology's\n+impairments, like `start` and `apply` do for local labs. A lab owned by a\n+Topology resource (the default) rejects `set` and `reset`: the clabernetes\n+controller renders its Links and reverts any direct change, so its impairments\n+come from the topology.\n+\n+Link impairments need a clabernetes release whose Link has an endpoint\n+`netem`. containerlab checks the published Link schema the first time a lab\n+uses them, because an older release would drop the field and deploy the lab\n+unimpaired. clabernetes programs the delay in 32-bit kernel ticks, so it\n+accepts delays up to `4m`.\n+\n ## Start, stop, and restart\n \n Node lifecycle commands ask the clabernetes controllers for a run state; they\n never touch Deployments or Pods.\n \n@@ -1413,19 +1448,18 @@ Known command differences:\n - Destroy flags `--graceful` and `--keep-mgmt-net` are rejected. `--cleanup`\n   also deletes the lab's persistent claims (saved device state) and removes\n   the local lab directory; a plain destroy keeps the claims.\n - Local Docker commands on the outer host are not authoritative for c9s labs.\n - `inspect interfaces` lists only the lab link interfaces (those `capture`\n-  accepts), not the management or pod interfaces. linkEndpointFields are the spec fields of a c9s Link's two endpoints.\n+var linkEndpointFields = []string{\"endpointA\", \"endpointB\"} //nolint:gochecknoglobals\n+\n+// SetImpairment sets the netem impairment of one lab link interface on the endpoint of its c9s\n+// Link, or removes it when the request carries none. The connectivity sidecar of the node's pod\n+// applies the change live; a later deploy restores the impairments the topology declares. A lab\n+// owned by a Topology resource is rejected: its controller renders the Links and reverts any\n+// direct change, so its impairments come from the topology.\n+func (r *Runtime) SetImpairment(\n+\tctx context.Context,\n+\treq clablabruntime.ImpairmentRequest,\n+) error {\n+\tr, err := r.connect(ctx, req.Identity)\n+\tif err != nil {\n+\t\treturn err\n+\t}\n+\n+\tif err = r.ensureLinkNetemSupport(ctx); err != nil {\n+\t\treturn err\n+\t}\n+\n+\tlocations, err := r.LocateNode(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{\n+\t\tName: req.Name, Namespace: req.Namespace, Nodes: []string{req.Node},\n+\t\tIdentity: req.Identity,\n+\t})\n+\tif err != nil {\n+\t\treturn err\n+\t}\n+\tlocation := locations[0]\n+\n+\t_, err = r.client.Resource(topologyGVR).Namespace(location.Namespace).\n+\t\tGet(ctx, req.Name, metav1.GetOptions{})\n+\tswitch {\n+\tcase err == nil:\n+\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"c9s lab %s/%s is owned by a Topology resource, whose controller \"+\n+\t\t\t\"reverts changes to its links; declare the impairment in the topology and deploy \"+\n+\t\t\t\"again, or deploy the lab with --no-topology-cr\", location.Namespace, req.Name)\n+\tcase !apierrors.IsNotFound(err):\n+\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"failed to get clabernetes topology %s/%s: %w\",\n+\t\t\tlocation.Namespace, req.Name, err)\n+\t}\n+\n+\tlinks, err := r.primitiveResourcesForTopology(ctx, linkGVR, req.Name, location.Namespace)\n+\tif err != nil {\n+\t\treturn err\n+\t}\n+\n+\tlink, endpoint, ok := 1929: +*** Comments ***
1930: +This suite tests link impairments with the c9s runtime: the topology's impairments become the
1931: +netem of the c9s Links and clabwire programs them on the receiving sidecar legs, and tools netem
1932: +changes the Links of a lab deployed with --no-topology-cr.
1933: +
1934: +
1935: +*** Settings ***
1936: +Library             OperatingSystem
1937: +Library             Process
1938: +Library             String
1939: +Resource            ../common.robot
1940: +
1941: +Suite Setup         Setup
1942: +Suite Teardown      Run Clab Command    destroy -t ${topo} --cleanup
1943: +Test Tags           clabernetes    c9s
1944: +
1945: +
1946: +*** Variables ***
1947: +${runtime}          c9s
1948: +${lab-name}         c9s-link-netem
1949: +${topo}             ${CURDIR}/03-link-netem.clab.yml
1950: +${lab-namespace}    c9s-${lab-name}
1951: +${server-label}     clab-node-name\=server
1952: +
1953: +
1954: +*** Test Cases ***
1955: +Deploy c9s lab with link impairments
1956: +    ${output} =    Run Clab Command    deploy -t ${topo}
1957: +    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${output.rc}    0
1958: +
1959: +The Link declares the topology's impairment
1960: +    ${links} =    Process.Run Process
1961: +    ...    kubectl -n ${lab-namespace} get links.c9s.run -l c9s.run/topologyOwner\=${lab-name} -o jsonpath\='{.items[*].spec.endpointA.netem.delay}'
1962: +    ...    shell=True
1963: +    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${links.rc}    0
1964: +    Should Be Equal    ${links.stdout}    50ms
1965: +
1966: +Clabwire programs the impairment on the receiving sidecar leg
1967: +    Wait Until Keyword Succeeds    120s    5s    Server Sidecar Qdisc Should Contain    delay 50ms
1968: +
1969: +Tools netem shows the impairment
1970: +    ${output} =    Run Clab Command    tools netem show -t ${topo} -n client -f json
1971: +    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${output.rc}    0
1972: +    Should Contain    ${output.stdout}    "delay": "50ms"
1973: +
1974: +Tools netem leaves a Topology-owned lab to the topology
1975: +    ${output} =    Run Clab Command    tools netem set -t ${topo} -n client -i eth1 --delay 200ms
1976: +    Should Not Be Equal As Integers    ${output.rc}    0
1977: +    Should Contain    ${output.stderr}    --no-topology-cr
1978: +
1979: +Deploy the lab without a Topology resource
1980: +    ${output} =    Run Clab Command    destroy -t ${topo} --cleanup
1981: +    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${output.rc}    0
1982: +    ${output} =    Run Clab Command    deploy -t ${topo} --no-topology-cr
1983: +    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${output.rc}    0
1984: +    Wait Until Keyword Succeeds    120s    5s    Server Sidecar Qdisc Should Contain    delay 50ms
1985: +
1986: +Tools netem changes the impairment live
1987: +    ${output} =    Run Clab Command    tools netem set -t ${topo} -n client -i eth1 --delay 200ms --loss 1
1988: +    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${output.rc}    0
1989: +    Should Contain    ${output.stdout}    200ms
1990: +    Wait Until Keyword Succeeds    180s    5s    Server Sidecar Qdisc Should Contain    delay 200ms
1991: +
1992: +Tools netem resets the impairment
1993: +    ${output} =    Run Clab Command    tools netem reset -t ${topo} -n client -i eth1
1994: +    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${output.rc}    0
1995: +    Wait Until Keyword Succeeds    180s    5s    Server Sidecar Should Have No Impairment
1996: +
1997: +A deploy restores the topology's impairments
1998: +    ${output} =    Run Clab Command    deploy -t ${topo} --no-topology-cr
1999: +    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${output.rc}    0
2000: +    Wait Until Keyword Succeeds    180s    5s    Server Sidecar Qdisc Should Contain    delay 50ms
2001: +
2002: +
2003: +*** Keywords ***
2004: +Setup
2005: +    Skip If    '${runtime}' != 'c9s'    This suite targets the c9s runtime.
2006: +    ${output} =    Run Clab Command    destroy -t ${topo} --cleanup
2007: +    Log    Cleanup return code: ${output.rc}
2008: +
2009: +Run Clab Command
2010: +    [Arguments]    ${args}
2011: +    ${output} =    Process.Run Process
2012: +    ...    ${CLAB_BIN} --runtime ${runtime} ${args}
2013: +    ...    shell=True
2014: +    Log    stdout:${\n}${output.stdout}    console=${True}
2015: +    Log    stderr:${\n}${output.stderr}    console=${True}
2016: +    RETURN    ${output}
2017: +
2018: +Server Sidecar Qdisc Should Contain
2019: +    [Arguments]    ${expected}
2020: +    ${output} =    Server Sidecar Qdiscs
2021: +    Should Contain    ${output.stdout}${output.stderr}    ${expected}
2022: +
2023: +Server Sidecar Should Have No Impairment
2024: +    ${output} =    Server Sidecar Qdiscs
2025: +    Should Not Contain    ${output.stdout}${output.stderr}    netem c9:
2026: +
2027: +Server Sidecar Qdiscs
2028: +    ${output} =    Run Clab Command
2029: +    ...    exec -t ${topo} --label ${server-label} --cmd 'tc qdisc show'
2030: +    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${output.rc}    0
2031: +    RETURN    ${output}

61: 		&o.ToolsNetem.Interface,
62: 		"interface",
63: 		"i",
64: 		o.ToolsNetem.Interface,
65: 		"interface to apply impairment to",
66: 	)
67: 	netemSetCmd.Flags().DurationVarP(
68: 		&o.ToolsNetem.Delay,
69: 		"delay",
70: 		"",
71: 		o.ToolsNetem.Delay,
72: 		"time to delay outgoing packets (e.g. 100ms, 2s)",
73: 	)
74: 	netemSetCmd.Flags().DurationVarP(
75: 		&o.ToolsNetem.Jitter,
76: 		"jitter",
77: 		"",
78: 		o.ToolsNetem.Jitter,
79: 		"delay variation, aka jitter (e.g. 50ms)",
80: 	)
81: 	netemSetCmd.Flags().Float64VarP(
82: 		&o.ToolsNetem.Loss,
83: 		"loss",
84: 		"",
85: 		o.ToolsNetem.Loss,
86: 		"random packet loss expressed in percentage (e.g. 0.1 means 0.1%)",
87: 	)
88: 	netemSetCmd.Flags().Uint64VarP(
89: 		&o.ToolsNetem.Rate,
90: 		"rate",
91: 		"",
92: 		o.ToolsNetem.Rate, "link rate limit in kbit")
93: 	netemSetCmd.Flags().Float64VarP(
94: 		&o.ToolsNetem.Corruption,
95: 		"corruption",
96: 		"",
97: 		0,
98: 		"random packet corruption probability expressed in percentage (e.g. 0.1 means 0.1%)",
99: 	)
100: 	netemSetCmd.MarkFlagRequired("interface")
101: 
102: 	netemShowCmd := &cobra.Command{
103: 		Use:   "show",
104: 		Short: "show link impairments for a node",
105: 		PreRunE: func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
106: 			return validateInputAndRoot(o)
107: 		},
108: 		RunE: func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
109: 			return netemShowFn(o)
110: 		},
111: 	}
112: 	c.AddCommand(netemShowCmd)
113: 	netemShowCmd.Flags().StringVarP(
114: 		&o.ToolsNetem.ContainerName,
115: 		"node",
116: 		"n",
117: 		o.ToolsNetem.ContainerName,
118: 		"node name from topology, or container name without --topo/--name",
119: 	)
120: 	netemShowCmd.Flags().StringVarP(
121: 		&o.ToolsNetem.Format,
122: 		"format",
123: 		"f",
124: 		o.ToolsNetem.Format,
125: 		"output format (table, json)",
126: 	)
127: 
128: 	netemResetCmd := &cobra.Command{
129: 		Use:   "reset",
130: 		Short: "reset link impairments",
131: 		Long:  `Reset network impairments by deleting the netem qdisc from the specified interface.`,
132: 		PreRunE: func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
133: 			return validateInputAndRoot(o)
134: 		},
135: 		RunE: func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
136: 			return netemResetFn(o)
137: 		},
138: 	}
139: 	c.AddCommand(netemResetCmd)
140: 	netemResetCmd.Flags().StringVarP(&o.ToolsNetem.ContainerName, "node", "n",
141: 		o.ToolsNetem.ContainerName, "node name from topology, or container name without --topo/--name")
142: 	netemResetCmd.Flags().StringVarP(&o.ToolsNetem.Interface, "interface", "i",
143: 		o.ToolsNetem.Interface, "interface to reset impairment on")
144: 	netemResetCmd.MarkFlagRequired("interface")
145: 
146: 	return c, nil
147: }

149: func netemSetFn(ctx context.Context, o *Options) error {
150: 	if o.ToolsNetem.ContainerName == "" {
151: 		return fmt.Errorf("--node/-n must be specified for 'set' command")
152: 	}
153: 
154: 	if netemLabRuntimeSelected(o) {
155: 		return netemSetLabRuntime(ctx, o)
156: 	}
157: 
158: 	// Ensure that the sch_netem kernel module is loaded (for Fedora/RHEL compatibility)
159: 	if err := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "modprobe", "sch_netem").Run(); err != nil {
160: 		log.Warn(
161: 			"failed to load sch_netem kernel module (expected on OrbStack machines)",
162: 			"err",
163: 			err,
164: 		)
165: 	}
166: 
167: 	node, err := resolveNetemNode(ctx, o)
168: 	if err != nil {
169: 		return err
170: 	}
171: 
172: 	target, err := node.TargetFor(o.ToolsNetem.Interface)
173: 	if err != nil {
174: 		return err
175: 	}
176: 
177: 	nodeNs, err := ns.GetNS(target.NSPath)
178: 	if err != nil {
179: 		return err
180: 	}
181: 
182: 	tcnl, err := clabnetem.NewTC(int(nodeNs.Fd()))
183: 	if err != nil {
184: 		return err
185: 	}
186: 
187: 	defer func() {
188: 		if err := tcnl.Close(); err != nil {
189: 			log.Errorf("could not close rtnetlink socket: %v\n", err)
190: 		}
191: 	}()
192: 
193: 	err = nodeNs.Do(func(_ ns.NetNS) error {
194: 		netemIfLink, err := netlink.LinkByName(
195: 			clabutils.SanitizeInterfaceName(target.Iface))
196: 		if err != nil {
197: 			return err
198: 		}
199: 
200: 		netemIfName := netemIfLink.Attrs().Name
201: 
202: 		link, err := net.InterfaceByName(netemIfName)
203: 		if err != nil {
204: 			return err
205: 		}
206: 
207: 		qdisc, err := clabnetem.SetImpairments(
208: 			tcnl,
209: 			target.DisplayName,
210: 			link,
211: 			o.ToolsNetem.Delay,
212: 			o.ToolsNetem.Jitter,
213: 			o.ToolsNetem.Loss,
214: 			o.ToolsNetem.Rate,
215: 			o.ToolsNetem.Corruption,
216: 		)
217: 		if err != nil {
218: 			return err
219: 		}
220: 
221: 		printImpairments([]tableWriter.Row{qdiscToTableData(qdisc)})
222: 
223: 		return nil
224: 	})
225: 
226: 	return err
227: }
228: 
229: func validateInputAndRoot(o *Options) error {
230: 	if o.ToolsNetem.Loss < 0 || o.ToolsNetem.Loss > 100 {
231: 		return fmt.Errorf("packet loss must be in the range between 0 and 100")
232: 	}
233: 
234: 	if o.ToolsNetem.Jitter != 0 && o.ToolsNetem.Delay == 0 {
235: 		return fmt.Errorf("jitter cannot be set without setting delay")
236: 	}
237: 
238: 	// a lab runtime changes its links through its API, not local network namespaces
239: 	if netemLabRuntimeSelected(o) {
240: 		return nil
241: 	}
242: 
243: 	if err := clabutils.CheckAndGetRootPrivs(); err != nil {
244: 		return err
245: 	}
246: 
247: 	return nil
248: }
249: 
250: func resolveNetemNode(ctx context.Context, o *Options) (*clabcore.NetemNode, error) {
251: 	if o.Global.TopologyFile != "" || o.Global.TopologyName != "" {
252: 		c, err := clabcore.NewContainerLab(o.ToClabOptions()...)
253: 		if err != nil {
254: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to load topology: %w", err)
255: 		}
256: 
257: 		node, err := c.GetNode(o.ToolsNetem.ContainerName)
258: 		if err != nil {
259: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf(
260: 				"node %q not found in topology: %w",
261: 				o.ToolsNetem.ContainerName,
262: 				err,
263: 			)
264: 		}
265: 
266: 		nsPath, err := node.GetNSPath(ctx)
267: 		if err != nil {
268: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf(
269: 				"failed to get namespace path for node %q: %w",
270: 				o.ToolsNetem.ContainerName,
271: 				err,
272: 			)
273: 		}
274: 		return clabcore.NewNetemNode(
275: 			nsPath,
276: 			o.ToolsNetem.ContainerName,
277: 			c.Config.Name,
278: 			o.ToolsNetem.ContainerName,
279: 		), nil
280: 	}
281: 
282: 	return clabcore.ResolveNetemNode(
283: 		ctx,
284: 		o.Global.Runtime,
285: 		o.Global.Timeout,
286: 		o.ToolsNetem.ContainerName,
287: 	)
288: }

290: func printImpairments(rows []tableWriter.Row) {
291: 	table := tableWriter.NewWriter()
292: 	table.SetOutputMirror(os.Stdout)
293: 	table.SetStyle(tableWriter.StyleRounded)
294: 	table.Style().Format.Header = text.FormatTitle
295: 	table.Style().Format.HeaderAlign = text.AlignCenter
296: 	table.Style().Color = tableWriter.ColorOptions{
297: 		Header: text.Colors{text.Bold},
298: 	}
299: 
300: 	header := tableWriter.Row{
301: 		"Interface",
302: 		"Delay",
303: 		"Jitter",
304: 		"Packet Loss",
305: 		"Rate (kbit)",
306: 		"Corruption",
307: 	}
308: 
309: 	table.AppendHeader(header)
310: 
311: 	table.AppendRows(rows)
312: 	table.Render()
313: }
314: 
315: func qdiscToTableData(qdisc *gotc.Object) tableWriter.Row {
316: 	link, err := netlink.LinkByIndex(int(qdisc.Ifindex))
317: 	if err != nil {
318: 		log.Errorf("could not get netlink interface by index: %v", err)
319: 	}
320: 
321: 	var delay, jitter, loss, rate, corruption string
322: 
323: 	ifDisplayName := link.Attrs().Name
324: 	if link.Attrs().Alias != "" {
325: 		ifDisplayName += fmt.Sprintf(" (%s)", link.Attrs().Alias)
326: 	}
327: 
328: 	// return N/A values when netem is not set
329: 	// which is the case when qdisc is not set for an interface
330: 	if qdisc.Netem == nil {
331: 		return tableWriter.Row{
332: 			ifDisplayName,
333: 			clabconstants.NotApplicable, // delay
334: 			clabconstants.NotApplicable, // jitter
335: 			clabconstants.NotApplicable, // loss
336: 			clabconstants.NotApplicable, // rate
337: 			clabconstants.NotApplicable, // corruption
338: 		}
339: 	}
340: 
341: 	if qdisc.Netem.Latency64 != nil {
342: 		delay = (time.Duration(*qdisc.Netem.Latency64) * time.Nanosecond).String()
343: 	}
344: 
345: 	if qdisc.Netem.Jitter64 != nil {
346: 		jitter = (time.Duration(*qdisc.Netem.Jitter64) * time.Nanosecond).String()
347: 	}
348: 
349: 	loss = strconv.FormatFloat(
350: 		float64(qdisc.Netem.Qopt.Loss)/float64(math.MaxUint32)*100, 'f', 2, 64,
351: 	) + "%"
352: 	rate = strconv.FormatUint(clabnetem.RateKbit(qdisc.Netem), 10)
353: 	corruption = strconv.FormatFloat(float64(qdisc.Netem.Corrupt.Probability)/
354: 		float64(math.MaxUint32)*100, 'f', 2, 64) + "%"
355: 
356: 	return tableWriter.Row{
357: 		ifDisplayName,
358: 		delay,
359: 		jitter,
360: 		loss,
361: 		rate,
362: 		corruption,
363: 	}
364: }
365: 
366: // qdiscToJSONData converts the full qdisc object to a simplified view.
367: func qdiscToJSONData(qdisc *gotc.Object) clabtypes.ImpairmentData {
368: 	link, err := netlink.LinkByIndex(int(qdisc.Ifindex))
369: 	if err != nil {
370: 		log.Errorf("could not get netlink interface by index: %v", err)
371: 	}
372: 
373: 	var delay, jitter string
374: 
375: 	var loss, corruption float64
376: 
377: 	var rate int
378: 
379: 	ifDisplayName := link.Attrs().Name
380: 	if link.Attrs().Alias != "" {
381: 		ifDisplayName += fmt.Sprintf(" (%s)", link.Attrs().Alias)
382: 	}
383: 
384: 	// Return "N/A" values when netem is not set.
385: 	if qdisc.Netem == nil {
386: 		return clabtypes.ImpairmentData{
387: 			Interface: ifDisplayName,
388: 		}
389: 	}
390: 
391: 	if qdisc.Netem.Latency64 != nil && *qdisc.Netem.Latency64 != 0 {
392: 		delay = (time.Duration(*qdisc.Netem.Latency64) * time.Nanosecond).String()
393: 	}
394: 
395: 	if qdisc.Netem.Jitter64 != nil && *qdisc.Netem.Jitter64 != 0 {
396: 		jitter = (time.Duration(*qdisc.Netem.Jitter64) * time.Nanosecond).String()
397: 	}
398: 
399: 	rate = int(clabnetem.RateKbit(qdisc.Netem))
400: 
401: 	if qdisc.Netem.Corrupt != nil && qdisc.Netem.Corrupt.Probability != 0 {
402: 		// round to 2 decimal places
403: 		corruption = math.Round((float64(qdisc.Netem.Corrupt.Probability)/
404: 			float64(math.MaxUint32)*100)*100) / 100 //nolint: mnd
405: 	}
406: 
407: 	if qdisc.Netem.Qopt.Loss != 0 {
408: 		// round to 2 decimal places
409: 		loss = math.Round(
410: 			(float64(qdisc.Netem.Qopt.Loss)/float64(math.MaxUint32)*100)*100) / 100 //nolint: mnd
411: 	}
412: 
413: 	return clabtypes.ImpairmentData{
414: 		Interface:  ifDisplayName,
415: 		Delay:      delay,
416: 		Jitter:     jitter,
417: 		PacketLoss: loss,
418: 		Rate:       rate,
419: 		Corruption: corruption,
420: 	}
421: }
422: 
423: func netemShowFn(o *Options) error {
424: 	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
425: 	defer cancel()
426: 
427: 	if netemLabRuntimeSelected(o) {
428: 		return netemShowLabRuntime(ctx, o)
429: 	}
430: 
431: 	if o.ToolsNetem.ContainerName == "" {
432: 		if o.Global.TopologyFile == "" && o.Global.TopologyName == "" {
433: 			return fmt.Errorf(
434: 				"either --node/-n or --topo/-t (to show all nodes) must be specified",
435: 			)
436: 		}
437: 		return netemShowAllNodesFn(ctx, o)
438: 	}
439: 
440: 	node, err := resolveNetemNode(ctx, o)
441: 	if err != nil {
442: 		return err
443: 	}
444: 
445: 	return showNodeImpairments(o, node, o.ToolsNetem.ContainerName)
446: }
447: 
448: func showNodeImpairments(
449: 	o *Options,
450: 	node *clabcore.NetemNode,
451: 	displayName string,
452: ) error {
453: 	nodeNs, err := ns.GetNS(node.NSPath)
454: 	if err != nil {
455: 		return err
456: 	}
457: 
458: 	tcnl, err := clabnetem.NewTC(int(nodeNs.Fd()))
459: 	if err != nil {
460: 		return err
461: 	}
462: 
463: 	defer func() {
464: 		if err := tcnl.Close(); err != nil {
465: 			log.Errorf("could not close rtnetlink socket: %v", err)
466: 		}
467: 	}()
468: 
469: 	jsonFormat := o.ToolsNetem.Format == clabconstants.FormatJSON
470: 
471: 	var impairments []clabtypes.ImpairmentData
472: 
473: 	var tableRows []tableWriter.Row
474: 
475: 	var ifaceNames []string
476: 
477: 	err = nodeNs.Do(func(_ ns.NetNS) error {
478: 		qdiscs, err := clabnetem.Impairments(tcnl)
479: 		if err != nil {
480: 			return err
481: 		}
482: 
483: 		for idx := range qdiscs {
484: 			if jsonFormat {
485: 				if qdiscs[idx].Attribute.Kind != "netem" {
486: 					continue // skip clsact or other qdisc types
487: 				}
488: 
489: 				impairments = append(impairments, qdiscToJSONData(&qdiscs[idx]))
490: 			} else {
491: 				tableRows = append(tableRows, qdiscToTableData(&qdiscs[idx]))
492: 			}
493: 		}
494: 
495: 		// Tools-interface lookups run in the host netns, outside this closure.
496: 		// A tools interface is published under the interface's topology-facing
497: 		// name: the alias when a kind remapped the interface name.
498: 		links, err := netlink.LinkList()
499: 		if err != nil {
500: 			return err
501: 		}
502: 
503: 		for _, l := range links {
504: 			name := l.Attrs().Alias
505: 			if name == "" {
506: 				name = l.Attrs().Name
507: 			}
508: 
509: 			ifaceNames = append(ifaceNames, name)
510: 		}
511: 
512: 		return nil
513: 	})
514: 	if err != nil {
515: 		return err
516: 	}
517: 
518: 	// Interfaces whose tools interface lives in the host netns carry their
519: 	// impairments there, not in the container netns.
520: 	hostImpairments, hostRows, err := toolsIfaceImpairments(node, ifaceNames)
521: 	if err != nil {
522: 		return err
523: 	}
524: 
525: 	impairments = append(impairments, hostImpairments...)
526: 	tableRows = append(tableRows, hostRows...)
527: 
528: 	if jsonFormat {
529: 		outputData := map[string][]clabtypes.ImpairmentData{
530: 			displayName: impairments,
531: 		}
532: 
533: 		jsonData, err := json.MarshalIndent(outputData, "", "  ")
534: 		if err != nil {
535: 			return fmt.Errorf("error marshaling JSON: %v", err)
536: 		}
537: 
538: 		fmt.Println(string(jsonData))
539: 	} else {
540: 		printImpairments(tableRows)
541: 	}
542: 
543: 	return nil
544: }
545: 
546: func netemShowAllNodesFn(ctx context.Context, o *Options) error {
547: 	c, err := clabcore.NewContainerLab(o.ToClabOptions()...)
548: 	if err != nil {
549: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to load topology: %w", err)
550: 	}
551: 
552: 	allImpairments := make(map[string][]clabtypes.ImpairmentData)
553: 
554: 	for nodeName, topologyNode := range c.Nodes {
555: 		nsPath, err := topologyNode.GetNSPath(ctx)
556: 		if err != nil {
557: 			log.Warnf("failed to get namespace path for node %q: %v", nodeName, err)
558: 			continue
559: 		}
560: 
561: 		node := clabcore.NewNetemNode(nsPath, nodeName, c.Config.Name, nodeName)
562: 		if o.ToolsNetem.Format == clabconstants.FormatJSON {
563: 			impairments, err := getNodeImpairments(node)
564: 			if err != nil {
565: 				log.Warnf("failed to get impairments for node %q: %v", nodeName, err)
566: 				continue
567: 			}
568: 			allImpairments[nodeName] = impairments
569: 		} else {
570: 			fmt.Printf("\n=== Node: %s ===\n", nodeName)
571: 			if err := showNodeImpairments(o, node, nodeName); err != nil {
572: 				log.Warnf("failed to show impairments for node %q: %v", nodeName, err)
573: 			}
574: 		}
575: 	}
576: 
577: 	if o.ToolsNetem.Format == clabconstants.FormatJSON {
578: 		jsonData, err := json.MarshalIndent(allImpairments, "", "  ")
579: 		if err != nil {
580: 			return fmt.Errorf("error marshaling JSON: %v", err)
581: 		}
582: 		fmt.Println(string(jsonData))
583: 	}
584: 
585: 	return nil
586: }
587: 
588: func getNodeImpairments(node *clabcore.NetemNode) ([]clabtypes.ImpairmentData, error) {
589: 	nodeNs, err := ns.GetNS(node.NSPath)
590: 	if err != nil {
591: 		return nil, err
592: 	}
593: 
594: 	tcnl, err := clabnetem.NewTC(int(nodeNs.Fd()))
595: 	if err != nil {
596: 		return nil, err
597: 	}
598: 
599: 	defer func() {
600: 		if err := tcnl.Close(); err != nil {
601: 			log.Errorf("could not close rtnetlink socket: %v", err)
602: 		}
603: 	}()
604: 
605: 	var impairments []clabtypes.ImpairmentData
606: 
607: 	var ifaceNames []string
608: 
609: 	err = nodeNs.Do(func(_ ns.NetNS) error {
610: 		qdiscs, err := clabnetem.Impairments(tcnl)
611: 		if err != nil {
612: 			return err
613: 		}
614: 
615: 		for idx := range qdiscs {
616: 			if qdiscs[idx].Attribute.Kind != "netem" {
617: 				continue
618: 			}
619: 			impairments = append(impairments, qdiscToJSONData(&qdiscs[idx]))
620: 		}
621: 
622: 		links, err := netlink.LinkList()
623: 		if err != nil {
624: 			return err
625: 		}
626: 
627: 		for _, link := range links {
628: 			name := link.Attrs().Alias
629: 			if name == "" {
630: 				name = link.Attrs().Name
631: 			}
632: 			ifaceNames = append(ifaceNames, name)
633: 		}
634: 
635: 		return nil
636: 	})
637: 	if err != nil {
638: 		return nil, err
639: 	}
640: 
641: 	hostImpairments, _, err := toolsIfaceImpairments(node, ifaceNames)
642: 	if err != nil {
643: 		return nil, err
644: 	}
645: 
646: 	return append(impairments, hostImpairments...), nil
647: }
648: 
649: // toolsIfaceImpairments returns JSON and table impairment rows for the
650: // interfaces whose tools interface lives in the host netns (see
651: // utils.StitchAltName).
652: func toolsIfaceImpairments(
653: 	node *clabcore.NetemNode,
654: 	ifaces []string,
655: ) ([]clabtypes.ImpairmentData, []tableWriter.Row, error) {
656: 	toolsIfaces := map[uint32]string{} // host ifindex -> display name
657: 
658: 	for _, iface := range ifaces {
659: 		toolsIface := node.ToolsIfaceFor(iface)
660: 		if toolsIface == "" {
661: 			continue
662: 		}
663: 
664: 		l, err := netlink.LinkByName(toolsIface)
665: 		if err != nil {
666: 			continue
667: 		}
668: 
669: 		toolsIfaces[uint32(l.Attrs().Index)] = fmt.Sprintf("%s (host)", iface)
670: 	}
671: 
672: 	if len(toolsIfaces) == 0 {
673: 		return nil, nil, nil
674: 	}
675: 
676: 	hostNs, err := ns.GetCurrentNS()
677: 	if err != nil {
678: 		return nil, nil, err
679: 	}
680: 
681: 	tcnl, err := clabnetem.NewTC(int(hostNs.Fd()))
682: 	if err != nil {
683: 		return nil, nil, err
684: 	}
685: 
686: 	defer func() {
687: 		if err := tcnl.Close(); err != nil {
688: 			log.Errorf("could not close rtnetlink socket: %v", err)
689: 		}
690: 	}()
691: 
692: 	qdiscs, err := clabnetem.Impairments(tcnl)
693: 	if err != nil {
694: 		return nil, nil, err
695: 	}
696: 
697: 	var impairments []clabtypes.ImpairmentData
698: 
699: 	var rows []tableWriter.Row
700: 
701: 	for idx := range qdiscs {
702: 		display, ok := toolsIfaces[qdiscs[idx].Ifindex]
703: 		if !ok || qdiscs[idx].Attribute.Kind != "netem" {
704: 			continue
705: 		}
706: 
707: 		d := qdiscToJSONData(&qdiscs[idx])
708: 		d.Interface = display
709: 		impairments = append(impairments, d)
710: 
711: 		row := qdiscToTableData(&qdiscs[idx])
712: 		row[0] = display
713: 		rows = append(rows, row)
714: 	}
715: 
716: 	return impairments, rows, nil
717: }
718: 
719: func netemResetFn(o *Options) error {
720: 	if o.ToolsNetem.ContainerName == "" {
721: 		return fmt.Errorf("--node/-n must be specified for 'reset' command")
722: 	}
723: 
724: 	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
725: 	defer cancel()
726: 
727: 	if netemLabRuntimeSelected(o) {
728: 		return netemResetLabRuntime(ctx, o)
729: 	}
730: 
731: 	node, err := resolveNetemNode(ctx, o)
732: 	if err != nil {
733: 		return err
734: 	}
735: 
736: 	target, err := node.TargetFor(o.ToolsNetem.Interface)
737: 	if err != nil {
738: 		return err
739: 	}
740: 
741: 	nodeNs, err := ns.GetNS(target.NSPath)
742: 	if err != nil {
743: 		return err
744: 	}
745: 
746: 	tcnl, err := clabnetem.NewTC(int(nodeNs.Fd()))
747: 	if err != nil {
748: 		return err
749: 	}
750: 
751: 	defer func() {
752: 		if err := tcnl.Close(); err != nil {
753: 			log.Errorf("could not close rtnetlink socket: %v\n", err)
754: 		}
755: 	}()
756: 
757: 	err = nodeNs.Do(func(_ ns.NetNS) error {
758: 		netemIfLink, err := netlink.LinkByName(
759: 			clabutils.SanitizeInterfaceName(target.Iface))
760: 		if err != nil {
761: 			return err
762: 		}
763: 		// Retrieve the standard net.Interface from the netlink.Link name.
764: 		netemIfIface, err := net.InterfaceByName(netemIfLink.Attrs().Name)
765: 		if err != nil {
766: 			return err
767: 		}
768: 
769: 		if err := clabnetem.DeleteImpairments(tcnl, netemIfIface); err != nil {
770: 			return err
771: 		}
772: 
773: 		fmt.Printf("Reset impairments on node %q, interface %q\n",
774: 			target.DisplayName, netemIfLink.Attrs().Name)
775: 
776: 		return nil
777: 	})
778: 
779: 	return err
780: }

Notable observations so far:

1. `netemSetLabRuntime`: after Set, prints only the impairment rows where `impairment.Interface == o.ToolsNetem.Interface`. If the impairment didn't stick (e.g., controller rejected or netem empty), no output — but SetImpairment would error. However: for `set` with all zeros (e.g. `tools netem set -n x -i eth1` with no impairment flags), the request has a non-nil Impairment with all zeros. `linkNetem` returns empty map `{}`. The merge patch sets `"netem": {}` — an empty map, not null. So `set` with no impairment values writes an empty netem object rather than resetting. Compare local semantics: local `tools netem set` with all zero values — what does `clabnetem.SetImpairments` do with all-zero? Probably sets a netem qdisc with no impairments or an error? Let's check `SetImpairments` in netem package. Actually more importantly: after `set` with zero values, the c9s Link would have `netem: {}` present, and `Impairments()` would... `netem` found with len 0 → skipped (`len(netem)==0` continue), so show wouldn't list it, but the Link still has `spec.endpointA.netem: {}` which clabwire might interpret as no impairment. And later `reset` uses nil → null → removed. Probably minor. But another issue: `netemSetLabRuntime` with zero impairment prints nothing (no matching row since netem {} skipped), while local prints a table with N/A. Minor UX difference.

2. Bigger issue: In `netemSetLabRuntime`, after setting, it calls `LinkImpairments` then prints rows matching interface. But if the set patch succeeded, the Link now has the netem; the Impairments call lists links with `len(netem) == 0` skipped. Fine.

3. `validateInputAndRoot` — for lab runtime, skips root privileges. But also `netemSetFn` checks `o.ToolsNetem.ContainerName == ""` before the branch. For `show` with lab runtime and no `-n`, requires topo. OK.

4. `netemShowLabRuntime` table output: when a specific node requested, no header; when all nodes, prints header per node. Local behavior: `netemShowAllNodesFn` prints header then per-node; single node prints table. Consistent.

5. JSON format difference: local `show -n node -f json` prints `{displayName: [...]}`. Lab runtime show prints same shape. Good.

6. `impairmentTableRow` for local show table vs local `qdiscToTableData`: local uses display name with alias; lab runtime uses `impairment.Interface` (the interface name as in the Link spec). Fine.

275: 				"from the topology file alone; use --offline, --dot, --mermaid or --drawio",
276: 			"graph", runtimeName)
277: 	}
278:

281: 		if labRuntimeFlagWasSet(cobraCmd, flagName) {
282: 			unsupported = append(unsupported, "--"+flagName)
283: 		}

290: 			strings.Join(unsupported, ", "),
291: 			cobraCmd.Name(),
292: 			runtimeName,
293: 		)
294: 	}
295: 
296: 	return nil
297: }

16: // The helpers in this file give library users per-node access to the lab selected by the CLab
17: // (its topology file or WithTopologyName). Node names are accepted as the topology file spells
18: // them or as a lab runtime sanitized them. Lab runtime calls act as the identity set with
19: // WithLabRuntimeIdentity.
20: 
21: // CheckLabRuntimeSupport checks that the cluster behind the lab runtime runs a controller release
22: // with the contract the runtime needs (for c9s: clabernetes with Node run state and the clabwire
23: // capture contract). Lab runtime operations run the same check before their first cluster call;
24: // servers call it to fail early. The error wraps labruntime.ErrUnsupportedRuntimeVersion when the
25: // release is too old.
26: func (c *CLab) CheckLabRuntimeSupport(ctx context.Context) error {
27: 	checker, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.SupportChecker](
28: 		c, "checking the lab runtime version")
29: 	if err != nil {
30: 		return err
31: 	}
32: 
33: 	return checker.CheckSupport(ctx, c.labRuntimeIdentity)
34: }

36: // LocateLabRuntimeNodes reports the workload (namespace, pod, primary device container, Node
37: // UID, exposed ports) of the given nodes, or of every node of the lab when none are given.
38: func (c *CLab) LocateLabRuntimeNodes(
39: 	ctx context.Context,
40: 	nodeNames ...string,
41: ) ([]clablabruntime.NodeLocation, error) {
42: 	locator, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodeLocator](c, "locating nodes")
43: 	if err != nil {
44: 		return nil, err
45: 	}
46: 	if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
47: 		return nil, err
48: 	}
49: 
50: 	return locator.LocateNode(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{
51: 		Name:     c.Config.Name,
52: 		Nodes:    nodeNames,
53: 		Identity: c.labRuntimeIdentity,
54: 	})
55: }
56: 
57: // AttachLabRuntimeNode runs an interactive command in a node's device container (or in
58: // req.Container) with stdin, an optional TTY and terminal resizing. The lab name and identity
59: // default to the CLab's. A command exiting nonzero returns a *labruntime.CommandExitError.
60: func (c *CLab) AttachLabRuntimeNode(
61: 	ctx context.Context,
62: 	req clablabruntime.AttachRequest,
63: 	streams clablabruntime.AttachStreams,
64: ) error {
65: 	attacher, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodeAttacher](c, "attaching to nodes")
66: 	if err != nil {
67: 		return err
68: 	}
69: 
70: 	if req.Name == "" {
71: 		if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
72: 			return err
73: 		}
74: 		req.Name = c.Config.Name
75: 	}
76: 	if req.Identity.IsZero() {
77: 		req.Identity = c.labRuntimeIdentity
78: 	}
79: 
80: 	return attacher.Attach(ctx, req, streams)
81: }
82: 
83: // DialLabRuntimeNodePort opens a connection to a TCP port of a node (SSH, web UIs) through the
84: // lab runtime, such as a Kubernetes port-forward.
85: func (c *CLab) DialLabRuntimeNodePort(
86: 	ctx context.Context,
87: 	nodeName string,
88: 	port int,
89: ) (net.Conn, error) {
90: 	forwarder, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodePortForwarder](
91: 		c, "port-forwarding to nodes")
92: 	if err != nil {
93: 		return nil, err
94: 	}
95: 	if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
96: 		return nil, err
97: 	}
98: 
99: 	return forwarder.DialPort(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{
100: 		Name:     c.Config.Name,
101: 		Nodes:    []string{nodeName},
102: 		Identity: c.labRuntimeIdentity,
103: 	}, port)
104: }
105: 
106: // SampleLabRuntimeNodeStats reports the CPU and memory usage of the lab's running nodes. It
107: // returns an error wrapping labruntime.ErrMetricsUnavailable when the cluster serves no resource
108: // metrics.
109: func (c *CLab) SampleLabRuntimeNodeStats(ctx context.Context) ([]clablabruntime.NodeStats, error) {
110: 	sampler, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodeStatsSampler](
111: 		c, "sampling node stats")
112: 	if err != nil {
113: 		return nil, err
114: 	}
115: 	if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
116: 		return nil, err
117: 	}
118: 
119: 	return sampler.SampleStats(ctx, clablabruntime.InspectRequest{
120: 		Name:     c.Config.Name,
121: 		Identity: c.labRuntimeIdentity,
122: 	})
123: }
124: 
125: // NodeLogOptions selects the node log NodeLogs writes.
126: type NodeLogOptions struct {
127: 	// NodeName is the node whose log is written.
128: 	NodeName string
129: 	// Container overrides a lab runtime node's primary device container. Local runtimes do
130: 	// not support it.
131: 	Container string
132: 	// Tail limits the output to the last lines of the log; nil writes the whole log.
133: 	Tail *int64
134: 	// Follow keeps writing new log lines until the context ends.
135: 	Follow bool
136: 	// Timestamps prefixes every line with its timestamp.
137: 	Timestamps bool
138: }
139: 
140: // NodeLogs writes the log of a lab node with every runtime: the container log with Docker and
141: // Podman, the device container log with a lab runtime. Lab runtimes write one combined stream to
142: // stdout.
143: func (c *CLab) NodeLogs(
144: 	ctx context.Context,
145: 	opts NodeLogOptions,
146: 	stdout, stderr io.Writer,
147: ) error {
148: 	if opts.NodeName == "" {
149: 		return fmt.Errorf("node name is required")
150: 	}
151: 	if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
152: 		return err
153: 	}
154: 
155: 	if c.LabRuntime != nil {
156: 		streamer, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodeLogStreamer](
157: 			c, "streaming node logs")
158: 		if err != nil {
159: 			return err
160: 		}
161: 
162: 		return streamer.StreamLogs(ctx, clablabruntime.LogRequest{
163: 			Name:       c.Config.Name,
164: 			NodeName:   opts.NodeName,
165: 			Container:  opts.Container,
166: 			Tail:       opts.Tail,
167: 			Follow:     opts.Follow,
168: 			Timestamps: opts.Timestamps,
169: 			Identity:   c.labRuntimeIdentity,
170: 		}, stdout)
171: 	}
172: 
173: 	if opts.Container != "" {
174: 		return fmt.Errorf("selecting a container is only supported with lab runtimes")
175: 	}
176: 
177: 	runtime, containerName, err := c.nodeContainer(ctx, opts.NodeName)
178: 	if err != nil {
179: 		return err
180: 	}
181: 
182: 	writer, ok := runtime.(clabruntime.ContainerLogWriter)
183: 	if !ok {
184: 		return fmt.Errorf("container runtime %q does not support node logs", runtime.GetName())
185: 	}
186: 
187: 	return writer.WriteContainerLogs(ctx, containerName, clabruntime.ContainerLogOptions{
188: 		Tail:       opts.Tail,
189: 		Follow:     opts.Follow,
190: 		Timestamps: opts.Timestamps,
191: 	}, stdout, stderr)
192: }
193: 
194: // nodeContainer finds the container of a lab node in the local container runtimes by the lab
195: // and node name labels.
196: func (c *CLab) nodeContainer(
197: 	ctx context.Context,
198: 	nodeName string,
199: ) (clabruntime.ContainerRuntime, string, error) {
200: 	filters := []*clabtypes.GenericFilter{
201: 		{
202: 			FilterType: "label",
203: 			Field:      clabconstants.Containerlab,
204: 			Operator:   "=",
205: 			Match:      c.Config.Name,
206: 		},
207: 		{
208: 			FilterType: "label",
209: 			Field:      clabconstants.NodeName,
210: 			Operator:   "=",
211: 			Match:      nodeName,
212: 		},
213: 	}
214: 
215: 	runtimeNames := make([]string, 0, len(c.Runtimes))
216: 	for name := range c.Runtimes {
217: 		runtimeNames = append(runtimeNames, name)
218: 	}
219: 	sort.Strings(runtimeNames)
220: 
221: 	for _, name := range runtimeNames {
222: 		runtime := c.Runtimes[name]
223: 
224: 		containers, err := runtime.ListContainers(ctx, filters)
225: 		if err != nil {
226: 			return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("could not list containers: %w", err)
227: 		}
228: 		if len(containers) != 0 && len(containers[0].Names) != 0 {
229: 			return runtime, containers[0].Names[0], nil
230: 		}
231: 	}
232: 
233: 	return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("%w: node %q of lab %q has no container",
234: 		ErrNodeNotFound, nodeName, c.Config.Name)
235: }
236: 
237: func (c *CLab) requireLabName() error {
238: 	if c.Config == nil || c.Config.Name == "" {
239: 		return fmt.Errorf("provide a lab name (--name) or a topology file (--topo)")
240: 	}
241: 
242: 	return nil
243: }
244: 
245: // labRuntimeCapability returns the CLab's lab runtime as an optional lab runtime interface.
246: func labRuntimeCapability[T any](c *CLab, operation string) (T, error) {
247: 	var zero T
248: 
249: 	if c.LabRuntime == nil {
250: 		return zero, fmt.Errorf("%s needs a lab runtime such as %q",
251: 			operation, clablabruntime.ClabernetesRuntimeName)
252: 	}
253: 
254: 	capability, ok := c.LabRuntime.(T)
255: 	if !ok {
256: 		return zero, fmt.Errorf("lab runtime %q does not support %s",
257: 			c.globalRuntimeName, operation)
258: 	}
259: 
260: 	return capability, nil
261: }

Reasoning
So in the Deploy path: if `existingTopology != nil` → `reconcileTopology`; if `!req.NoTopologyCR` → `deployTopology` (controller renders Links). Only the `--no-topology-cr` path checks `linksDeclareNetem`.

In the topology-CR path, containerlab sends the rendered topology definition (with netem) to the controller; the controller (old release) renders Links without netem. So an older clabernetes release silently deploys the lab without impairments in the topology-CR path. That's the exact failure mode described for the check. But — in the topology-CR path, would an old controller even accept the netem key in the topology YAML? 81: // runtime rejects them client-side before anything is created.

90: // validatePrimitiveNodeKinds rejects pseudo-node kinds that cannot be realized by c9s.
91: func validatePrimitiveNodeKinds(primitives *primitiveResourceSet) error {
92: 	var unsupported []string
93: 	for _, node := range primitives.nodes {
94: 		kind, _, _ := unstructured.NestedString(node.Object, "spec", "kind")
95: 		reason, isUnsupported := unsupportedC9sNodeKinds[kind]
96: 		if !isUnsupported {
97: 			continue
98: 		}
99: 		unsupported = append(unsupported, fmt.Sprintf(
100: 			"node %q uses pseudo-node kind %q: %s", node.GetName(), kind, reason))
101: 	}
102: 	if len(unsupported) == 0 {
103: 		return nil
104: 	}
105: 	sort.Strings(unsupported)
106: 
107: 	return fmt.Errorf("topology contains features unsupported by c9s: %s",
108: 		strings.Join(unsupported, "; "))
109: }

113: // a DNS-1035 label. Node names are sanitized while the topology is staged, so this is the
114: // backstop that keeps the deploy fail-closed instead of surfacing an opaque API-server rejection
115: // after some resources were already created.
116: func validatePrimitiveNodeNames(primitives *primitiveResourceSet) error {
117: 	var invalid []string
118: 	for _, node := range primitives.nodes {
119: 		name := node.GetName()
120: 		if errs := validation.IsDNS1035Label(name); len(errs) != 0 {
121: 			invalid = append(invalid, fmt.Sprintf("%s (%s)", name, errs[0]))

123: 	}
124: 	if len(invalid) == 0 {
125: 		return nil
126: 	}
127: 	sort.Strings(invalid)
128: 
129: 	return fmt.Errorf(
130: 		"c9s node names must be lowercase RFC 1035 labels "+

132: 		strings.Join(invalid, "; "),

376: 		for name, actual := range existing[group.gvr] {
377: 			if actual.GetLabels()[labelTopologyOwner] != topologyName {
378: 				continue
379: 			}
380: 			if _, keep := desiredNames[group.gvr][name]; !keep {
381: 				appendPlanChange(plan, clablabruntime.ChangeDelete, group.kind, namespace, name)
382: 			}
383: 		}
384: 	}
385: 
386: 	if err := r.planNodeLinkEffects(ctx, namespace, topologyName, desired, plan); err != nil {
387: 		return err
388: 	}
389: 
390: 	return nil
391: }

393: func (r *Runtime) planConfigMaps(
394: 	ctx context.Context,
395: 	namespace,
396: 	topologyName string,
397: 	desired []stagedConfigMap,
398: 	plan *clablabruntime.DeployPlan,
399: ) error {
400: 	existingList, err := r.kubeClient.CoreV1().ConfigMaps(namespace).List(
401: 		ctx,
402: 		metav1.ListOptions{LabelSelector: labels.Set{labelTopologyOwner: topologyName}.String()},
403: 	)
404: 	if err != nil {
405: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to list staged ConfigMaps for c9s lab %s/%s: %w",
406: 			namespace, topologyName, err)
407: 	}
408: 	existing := make(map[string]*corev1.ConfigMap, len(existingList.Items))
409: 	for idx := range existingList.Items {
410: 		existing[existingList.Items[idx].Name] = &existingList.Items[idx]
411: 	}
412: 
413: 	desiredNames := make(map[string]struct{}, len(desired))
414: 	for _, staged := range desired {
415: 		desiredNames[staged.name] = struct{}{}
416: 		wanted := stagedConfigMapObject(namespace, topologyName, staged, nil)
417: 		actual := existing[staged.name]
418: 		if actual == nil {
419: 			appendPlanChange(plan, clablabruntime.ChangeCreate, "ConfigMap", namespace, staged.name)
420: 			continue
421: 		}
422: 
423: 		updated := actual.DeepCopy()
424: 		updated.Labels = mergeDesiredMetadata(actual.Labels, wanted.Labels)
425: 		updated.Data = wanted.Data
426: 		updated.BinaryData = wanted.BinaryData
427: 		if !stagedConfigMapsConform(actual, updated) {
428: 			appendPlanChange(plan, clablabruntime.ChangeUpdate, "ConfigMap", namespace, staged.name)
429: 		}
430: 	}
431: 
432: 	for name := range existing {
433: 		if _, keep := desiredNames[name]; !keep {
434: 			appendPlanChange(plan, clablabruntime.ChangeDelete, "ConfigMap", namespace, name)
435: 		}
436: 	}
437: 
438: 	return nil
439: }

441: func appendPlanChange(
442: 	plan *clablabruntime.DeployPlan,
443: 	action clablabruntime.ChangeAction,
444: 	kind,
445: 	namespace,
446: 	name string,
447: ) {
448: 	plan.Changes = append(plan.Changes, clablabruntime.ResourceChange{
449: 		Action: action, Kind: kind, Namespace: namespace, Name: name,
450: 	})
451: }

453: func sortDeployPlan(plan *clablabruntime.DeployPlan) {
454: 	sort.Slice(plan.Changes, func(i, j int) bool {
455: 		left, right := plan.Changes[i], plan.Changes[j]
456: 		if left.Action != right.Action {
457: 			return left.Action < right.Action
458: 		}
459: 		if left.Kind != right.Kind {
460: 			return left.Kind < right.Kind
461: 		}
462: 		if left.Namespace != right.Namespace {
463: 			return left.Namespace < right.Namespace
464: 		}
465: 
466: 		return left.Name < right.Name
467: 	})
468: }
