470: // planNodeLinkEffects reports the pod-level impact of the link changes a deploy brings:
471: // a node whose links change has its Pod replaced unless its link apply mode is live. The
472: // plan carries the resource-level changes of the links themselves, so this only adds the
473: // lifecycle entries the resource view hides, most notably the reboot of VM-backed nodes.
474: func (r *Runtime) planNodeLinkEffects(
475: 	ctx context.Context,
476: 	namespace,
477: 	topologyName string,
478: 	desired *primitiveResourceSet,
479: 	plan *clablabruntime.DeployPlan,
480: ) error {
481: 	desiredLinks := make(map[string]*unstructured.Unstructured, len(desired.links))
482: 	for _, link := range desired.links {
483: 		desiredLinks[link.GetName()] = link
484: 	}
485: 
486: 	existingLinks, err := r.client.Resource(linkGVR).Namespace(namespace).
487: 		List(ctx, metav1.ListOptions{
488: 			LabelSelector: labels.Set{labelTopologyOwner: topologyName}.String(),
489: 		})
490: 	if err != nil {
491: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to list c9s links in namespace %s: %w", namespace, err)
492: 	}
493: 
494: 	existingLinkByName := make(map[string]*unstructured.Unstructured, len(existingLinks.Items))
495: 	for idx := range existingLinks.Items {
496: 		existingLinkByName[existingLinks.Items[idx].GetName()] = &existingLinks.Items[idx]
497: 	}
498: 
499: 	affected := map[string]struct{}{}
500: 	for _, desiredLink := range desired.links {
501: 		existing := existingLinkByName[desiredLink.GetName()]
502: 		if existing == nil {
503: 			collectAffectedLinkNodes(desiredLink, affected)
504: 
505: 			continue
506: 		}
507: 		if linkSpecsConform(existing, desiredLink) {
508: 			continue
509: 		}
510: 
511: 		// A rewired link tears down both sides: the previous endpoint loses its
512: 		// interface, the new one gains it.
513: 		collectAffectedLinkNodes(desiredLink, affected)
514: 		collectAffectedLinkNodes(existing, affected)
515: 	}
516: 	for name, existingLink := range existingLinkByName {
517: 		if _, keep := desiredLinks[name]; keep {
518: 			continue
519: 		}
520: 		collectAffectedLinkNodes(existingLink, affected)
521: 	}
522: 
523: 	if len(affected) == 0 {
524: 		return nil
525: 	}
526: 
527: 	// A Pod replacement only concerns nodes that exist and are still desired: brand new
528: 	// nodes come up with the new wiring already in place, and removed nodes lose their
529: 	// Pod entirely.
530: 	existingNodes, err := r.client.Resource(nodeGVR).Namespace(namespace).
531: 		List(ctx, metav1.ListOptions{
532: 			LabelSelector: labels.Set{labelTopologyOwner: topologyName}.String(),
533: 		})
534: 	if err != nil {
535: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to list c9s nodes in namespace %s: %w", namespace, err)
536: 	}
537: 
538: 	existingNodeByName := make(map[string]struct{}, len(existingNodes.Items))
539: 	for idx := range existingNodes.Items {
540: 		existingNodeByName[existingNodes.Items[idx].GetName()] = struct{}{}
541: 	}
542: 
543: 	for _, node := range desired.nodes {
544: 		name := node.GetName()
545: 		if _, ok := affected[name]; !ok {
546: 			continue
547: 		}
548: 		if _, running := existingNodeByName[name]; !running {
549: 			continue
550: 		}
551: 
552: 		mode, err := r.nodeLinkApplyMode(node)
553: 		if err != nil {
554: 			return err
555: 		}
556: 		if mode == clabtypes.LinkApplyModeLive {
557: 			continue
558: 		}
559: 
560: 		// c9s replaces the Pod for both the restart and the recreate mode; only live
561: 		// changes keep the Pod in place.
562: 		appendPlanChange(plan, clablabruntime.ChangeRecreate, "Pod", namespace, name)
563: 	}
564: 
565: 	return nil
566: }

568: // collectAffectedLinkNodes adds both sides of a Link to the set of nodes whose Pod the
569: // link change replaces.
570: func collectAffectedLinkNodes(link *unstructured.Unstructured, affected map[string]struct{}) {
571: 	for _, side := range []string{"endpointA", "endpointB"} {
572: 		nodeName, _, _ := unstructured.NestedString(link.Object, "spec", side, "nodeName")
573: 		if nodeName == "" || nodeName == "host" {
574: 			continue
575: 		}
576: 		affected[nodeName] = struct{}{}
577: 	}
578: }

580: // linkSpecsConform reports whether the stored Link spec matches the desired one, modulo
581: // API-defaulted empty values. Labels and annotations do not carry a wire, so only the
582: // spec decides whether a link changed.
583: func linkSpecsConform(existing, desired *unstructured.Unstructured) bool {
584: 	return apiequality.Semantic.DeepEqual(
585: 		normalizeAPIDefaultedJSON(existing.Object["spec"]),
586: 		normalizeAPIDefaultedJSON(desired.Object["spec"]),
587: 	)
588: }
589: 
590: // nodeLinkApplyMode resolves the link apply mode a c9s node uses when its links change:
591: // the topology's link-apply-mode override when set, otherwise the kind's default. Without
592: // a kind resolver the conservative recreate default applies to every affected node.
593: func (r *Runtime) nodeLinkApplyMode(
594: 	node *unstructured.Unstructured,
595: ) (clabtypes.LinkApplyMode, error) {
596: 	if override, _, _ := unstructured.NestedString(
597: 		node.Object, "spec", "link-apply-mode",
598: 	); override != "" {
599: 		mode := clabtypes.LinkApplyMode(override)
600: 		switch mode {
601: 		case clabtypes.LinkApplyModeLive, clabtypes.LinkApplyModeRestart,
602: 			clabtypes.LinkApplyModeRecreate:
603: 			return mode, nil
604: 		default:
605: 			return "", fmt.Errorf("node %q: invalid link-apply-mode %q", node.GetName(), override)
606: 		}
607: 	}
608: 
609: 	if r.kindLinkApplyMode == nil {
610: 		return clabtypes.LinkApplyModeRecreate, nil
611: 	}
612: 
613: 	mode := r.kindLinkApplyMode(nodeSpecKind(node))
614: 	if mode == "" {
615: 		return clabtypes.LinkApplyModeRecreate, nil
616: 	}
617: 
618: 	return clabtypes.LinkApplyMode(mode), nil
619: }
620: 
621: // nodeSpecKind returns the kind the compiled Node spec carries.
622: func nodeSpecKind(node *unstructured.Unstructured) string {
623: 	kind, _, _ := unstructured.NestedString(node.Object, "spec", "kind")
624: 
625: 	return kind
626: }

Now let me look at netem.go head (full), support.go head (full), clabernetes.go head relevant sections, and check where the netem check is missing for the topology-CR deploy path. Also confirm whether the topology-CR path even supports netem: `reconcileTopology`/`deployTopology` sends the Topology with the definition (including netem), and the controller compiles it. So the netem support check for topology-CR deploys would need to check the topology definition rather than primitives.links. The PR only checks primitives.links (compiled links) in the no-topology-cr branch. So a topology with netem deployed via the default path on an old clabernetes (< 0.12) silently deploys without impairments — the exact failure mode the new check prevents. Let me double check whether there's another gate: does `checkLabRuntimeLinkImpairments` in core get invoked on the deploy path for c9s? Yes (deployWithLabRuntime → checkLabRuntimeLinkImpairments), but it now returns nil for LinkImpairer implementers. So nothing else checks.

Hmm, wait. But could containerlab even validate topology-CR deploys for netem support? Yes: `if linksDeclareNetem(primitives.links)` — primitives.links is compiled from the topology in BOTH paths (prepareDesiredDeployment always compiles primitives). So the same `linksDeclareNetem(primitives.links)` check would work for both paths; it's just placed after the early return `if !req.NoTopologyCR { return r.deployTopology(...) }`. Moving the check before the branch (or into deployTopology/reconcileTopology) would close it. This is a solid P2 finding.

Wait, but is it a defect for reconcileTopology (existing topology)? Same: reconcileTopology updates the Topology; controller re-renders links; netem dropped on old release. Also gap.

Let me now read netem.go head fully to double-check details, and support.go.

153: 			return nodeImpairments[i].Interface < nodeImpairments[j].Interface
154: 		})
155: 
156: 		result = append(result, clablabruntime.NodeImpairments{
157: 			Node:        names.display(location.NodeName),
158: 			Impairments: nodeImpairments,
159: 		})
160: 	}
161: 
162: 	sort.Slice(result, func(i, j int) bool { return result[i].Node < result[j].Node })
163: 
164: 	return result, nil
165: }
166: 
167: // linksDeclareNetem reports whether any of the Links impairs one of its endpoints.
168: func linksDeclareNetem(links []*unstructured.Unstructured) bool {
169: 	for _, link := range links {
170: 		for _, endpoint := range linkEndpointFields {
171: 			if _, found, _ := unstructured.NestedFieldNoCopy(link.Object,
172: 				"spec", endpoint, "netem"); found {
173: 				return true
174: 			}
175: 		}
176: 	}
177: 
178: 	return false
179: }
180: 
181: // linkEndpoint finds the c9s Link with an endpoint on the node's interface and returns it with
182: // the spec field of that endpoint.
183: func linkEndpoint(
184: 	links []unstructured.Unstructured,
185: 	node,
186: 	iface string,
187: ) (*unstructured.Unstructured, string, bool) {
188: 	for idx := range links {
189: 		for _, endpoint := range linkEndpointFields {
190: 			endpointNode, _, _ := unstructured.NestedString(links[idx].Object,
191: 				"spec", endpoint, "nodeName")
192: 			endpointIface, _, _ := unstructured.NestedString(links[idx].Object,
193: 				"spec", endpoint, "interfaceName")
194: 
195: 			if endpointNode == node && endpointIface == iface {
196: 				return &links[idx], endpoint, true
197: 			}
198: 		}
199: 	}
200: 
201: 	return nil, "", false
202: }
203: 
204: // linkNetem renders an impairment in the c9s Link vocabulary, which is containerlab's.
205: func linkNetem(impairment *clablabruntime.Impairment) map[string]any {
206: 	netem := map[string]any{}
207: 
208: 	if impairment.Delay != 0 {
209: 		netem["delay"] = impairment.Delay.String()
210: 	}
211: 	if impairment.Jitter != 0 {
212: 		netem["jitter"] = impairment.Jitter.String()
213: 	}
214: 	if impairment.Loss != 0 {
215: 		netem["loss"] = impairment.Loss
216: 	}
217: 	if impairment.Rate != 0 {
218: 		netem["rate"] = impairment.Rate
219: 	}
220: 	if impairment.Corruption != 0 {
221: 		netem["corruption"] = impairment.Corruption
222: 	}
223: 
224: 	return netem
225: }
226: 
227: // impairmentData converts a c9s Link endpoint netem into the shape tools netem show reports for
228: // local labs.
229: func impairmentData(iface string, netem map[string]any) clabtypes.ImpairmentData {
230: 	data := clabtypes.ImpairmentData{Interface: iface}
231: 
232: 	if delay, ok := netem["delay"].(string); ok {
233: 		data.Delay = normalizedDuration(delay)
234: 	}
235: 	if jitter, ok := netem["jitter"].(string); ok {
236: 		data.Jitter = normalizedDuration(jitter)
237: 	}
238: 
239: 	data.PacketLoss = roundedPercent(netem["loss"])
240: 	data.Corruption = roundedPercent(netem["corruption"])
241: 
242: 	switch rate := netem["rate"].(type) {
243: 	case int64:
244: 		data.Rate = int(rate)
245: 	case float64:
246: 		data.Rate = int(rate)
247: 	}
248: 
249: 	return data
250: }
251: 
252: func normalizedDuration(value string) string {
253: 	duration, err := time.ParseDuration(value)
254: 	if err != nil {
255: 		return value
256: 	}
257: 
258: 	return duration.String()
259: }
260: 
261: // roundedPercent rounds a percentage to 2 decimal places, like tools netem show.
262: func roundedPercent(value any) float64 {
263: 	var percent float64
264: 
265: 	switch typed := value.(type) {
266: 	case int64:
267: 		percent = float64(typed)
268: 	case float64:
269: 		percent = typed
270: 	}
271: 
272: 	return math.Round(percent*100) / 100 //nolint:mnd
273: }

unstructured.NestedFieldNoCopy(link.Object,\n\t\t\t\t\"spec\", endpoint, \"netem\"); found {\n\t\t\t\treturn true\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn false\n}\n\n// linkEndpoint finds the c9s Link with an endpoint on the node's interface and returns it with\n// the spec field of that endpoint.\nfunc linkEndpoint(\n\tlinks []unstructured.Unstructured,\n\tnode,\n\tiface string,\n) (*unstructured.Unstructured, string, bool) {\n\tfor idx := range links {\n\t\tfor _, endpoint := range linkEndpointFields {\n\t\t\tendpointNode, _, _ := unstructured.NestedString(links[idx].Object,\n\t\t\t\t\"spec\", endpoint, \"nodeName\")\n\t\t\tendpointIface, _, _ := unstructured.NestedString(links[idx].Object,\n\t\t\t\t\"spec\", endpoint, \"interfaceName\")\n\n\t\t\tif endpointNode == node && endpointIface == iface {\n\t\t\t\treturn &links[idx], endpoint, true\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil, \"\", false\n}\n\n// linkNetem renders an impairment in the c9s Link vocabulary, which is containerlab's.\nfunc linkNetem(impairment *clablabruntime.Impairment) map[string]any {\n\tnetem := map[string]any{}\n\n\tif impairment.Delay != 0 {\n\t\tnetem[\"delay\"] = impairment.Delay.String()\n\t}\n\tif impairment.Jitter != 0 {\n\t\tnetem[\"jitter\"] = impairment.Jitter.String()\n\t}\n\tif impairment.Loss != 0 {\n\t\tnetem[\"loss\"] = impairment.Loss\n\t}\n\tif impairment.Rate != 0 {\n\t\tnetem[\"rate\"] = impairment.Rate\n\t}\n\tif impairment.Corruption != 0 {\n\t\tnetem[\"corruption\"] = impairment.Corruption\n\t}\n\n\treturn netem\n}\n\n// impairmentData converts a c9s Link endpoint netem into the shape tools netem show reports for\n// local labs.\nfunc impairmentData(iface string, netem map[string]any) clabtypes.ImpairmentData {\n\tdata := clabtypes.ImpairmentData{Interface: iface}\n\n\tif delay, ok := netem[\"delay\"].(string); ok {\n\t\tdata.Delay = normalizedDuration(delay)\n\t}\n\tif jitter, ok := netem[\"jitter\"].(string); ok {\n\t\tdata.Jitter = normalizedDuration(jitter)\n\t}\n\n\tdata.PacketLoss = roundedPercent(netem[\"loss\"])\n\tdata.Corruption = roundedPercent(netem[\"corruption\"])\n\n\tswitch rate := netem[\"rate\"].(type) {\n\tcase int64:\n\t\tdata.Rate = int(rate)\n\tcase float64:\n\t\tdata.Rate = int(rate)\n\t}\n\n\treturn data\n}\n\nfunc normalizedDuration(value string) string {\n\tduration, err := time.ParseDuration(value)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn value\n\t}\n\n\treturn duration.String()\n}\n\n// roundedPercent rounds a percentage to 2 decimal places, like tools netem show.\nfunc roundedPercent(value any) float64 {\n\tvar percent float64\n\n\tswitch typed := value.(type) {\n\tcase int64:\n\t\tpercent = float64(typed)\n\tcase float64:\n\t\tpercent = typed\n\t}\n\n\treturn math.Round(percent*100) / 100 //nolint:mnd\n}",

290: // once per runtime instance; servers call it at startup to fail early.

516: 	Interfaces []string
517: 	// From and To bound the gap on the node's clock; To is zero when it is unknown.
518: 	From   time.Time
519: 	To     time.Time
520: 	Reason string
521: }
522: 
523: // PacketCapturer streams pcapng from lab link interfaces. Capture writes one section with one
524: // Interface Description Block per target, named <node>:<interface>, before any packet. It
525: // returns when Duration passed, PacketLimit packets were written, or the context ended (which
526: // is not an error); the output is a valid capture whenever it stops.
527: type PacketCapturer interface {
528: 	CaptureInterfaces(ctx context.Context, req NodeRequest) ([]CaptureInterface, error)
529: 	Capture(ctx context.Context, req CaptureRequest, w io.Writer) error
530: }
531: 
532: // Impairment is the link impairment of the packets a lab link interface sends, with the values
533: // tools netem set takes.
534: type Impairment struct {
535: 	Delay      time.Duration
536: 	Jitter     time.Duration
537: 	Loss       float64
538: 	Rate       uint64
539: 	Corruption float64
540: }
541: 
542: // ImpairmentRequest sets the impairment of one lab link interface.
543: type ImpairmentRequest struct {
544: 	// Name is the lab name.
545: 	Name      string
546: 	Namespace string
547: 	// Node is the node name as the topology spells it.
548: 	Node      string
549: 	Interface string

551: 	Impairment *Impairment
552: 	// Identity overrides the runtime's configured identity for this call.
553: 	Identity Identity
554: }
555: 
556: // NodeImpairments is the impairment of each impaired lab link interface of a node.
557: type NodeImpairments struct {
558: 	// Node is the node name as the topology spells it.
559: 	Node        string
560: 	Impairments []clabtypes.ImpairmentData
561: }
562: 
563: // LinkImpairer sets and lists the link impairments of a lab's link interfaces, like tools netem
564: // does for local labs. Empty NodeRequest.Nodes lists every node of the lab.
565: type LinkImpairer interface {
566: 	SetImpairment(ctx context.Context, req ImpairmentRequest) error
567: 	Impairments(ctx context.Context, req NodeRequest) ([]NodeImpairments, error)
568: }
569: 
570: // InterfaceInspector lists the link interfaces of a lab's nodes with their current state, in the
571: // shape of `inspect interfaces`.
572: type InterfaceInspector interface {
573: 	InspectInterfaces(
574: 		ctx context.Context,
575: 		req NodeRequest,
576: 	) ([]*clabtypes.ContainerInterfaces, error)
577: }
578: 
579: // NodeStatsSampler reports the resource usage of a lab's nodes. It returns an error wrapping
580: // ErrMetricsUnavailable when the cluster serves no resource metrics.
581: type NodeStatsSampler interface {
582: 	SampleStats(ctx context.Context, req InspectRequest) ([]NodeStats, error)
583: }
584:

587: 	Destroy(context.Context, DestroyRequest) error

147: +package cmd
148: +
149: +import (
150: +	"context"
151: +	"encoding/json"
152: +	"fmt"
153: +	"strconv"
154: +
155: +	tableWriter "github.com/jedib0t/go-pretty/v6/table"
156: +	clabconstants "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/constants"
157: +	clabcore "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/core"
158: +	clablabruntime "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/labruntime"
159: +	clabtypes "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/types"
160: +)
161: +
162: +// netemLabRuntimeSelected reports whether tools netem runs with a lab runtime, which sets the
163: +// impairments on the runtime's links instead of in local network namespaces.
164: +func netemLabRuntimeSelected(o *Options) bool {
165: +	return clablabruntime.IsLabRuntimeName(o.Global.Runtime)
166: +}
167: +
168: +func netemLab(o *Options) (*clabcore.CLab, error) {
169: +	if o.Global.TopologyFile == "" && o.Global.TopologyName == "" {
170: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("--topo/-t or --name is required with lab runtime %q",
171: +			o.Global.Runtime)
172: +	}
173: +
174: +	c, err := clabcore.NewContainerLab(o.ToClabOptions()...)
175: +	if err != nil {
176: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to load topology: %w", err)
177: +	}
178: +
179: +	return c, nil
180: +}
181: +
182: +func netemSetLabRuntime(ctx context.Context, o *Options) error {
183: +	c, err := netemLab(o)
184: +	if err != nil {
185: +		return err
186: +	}
187: +
188: +	err = c.SetLinkImpairment(ctx, clablabruntime.ImpairmentRequest{
189: +		Node:      o.ToolsNetem.ContainerName,
190: +		Interface: o.ToolsNetem.Interface,
191: +		Impairment: &clablabruntime.Impairment{
192: +			Delay:      o.ToolsNetem.Delay,
193: +			Jitter:     o.ToolsNetem.Jitter,
194: +			Loss:       o.ToolsNetem.Loss,
195: +			Rate:       o.ToolsNetem.Rate,
196: +			Corruption: o.ToolsNetem.Corruption,
197: +		},
198: +	})
199: +	if err != nil {
200: +		return err
201: +	}
202: +
203: +	nodes, err := c.LinkImpairments(ctx, []string{o.ToolsNetem.ContainerName})
204: +	if err != nil {
205: +		return err
206: +	}
207: +
208: +	for _, node := range nodes {
209: +		for _, impairment := range node.Impairments {
210: +			if impairment.Interface == o.ToolsNetem.Interface {
211: +				printImpairments([]tableWriter.Row{impairmentTableRow(impairment)})
212: +			}
213: +		}
214: +	}
215: +
216: +	return nil
217: +}
218: +
219: +func netemShowLabRuntime(ctx context.Context, o *Options) error {
220: +	c, err := netemLab(o)
221: +	if err != nil {
222: +		return err
223: +	}
224: +
225: +	var requested []string
226: +	if o.ToolsNetem.ContainerName != "" {
227: +		requested = []string{o.ToolsNetem.ContainerName}
228: +	}
229: +
230: +	nodes, err := c.LinkImpairments(ctx, requested)
231: +	if err != nil {
232: +		return err
233: +	}
234: +
235: +	if o.ToolsNetem.Format == clabconstants.FormatJSON {
236: +		impairments := make(map[string][]clabtypes.ImpairmentData, len(nodes))
237: +		for _, node := range nodes {
238: +			impairments[node.Node] = node.Impairments
239: +		}
240: +
241: +		jsonData, err := json.MarshalIndent(impairments, "", "  ")
242: +		if err != nil {
243: +			return fmt.Errorf("error marshaling JSON: %v", err)
244: +		}
245: +
246: +		fmt.Println(string(jsonData))
247: +
248: +		return nil
249: +	}

512: @@ -701,10 +701,45 @@ Capturing needs `get` and `create` on `pods/exec` in the lab namespace, which
513:  `clabernetes-lab-editor` grants. `inspect interfaces -r c9s` lists the same
514:  interfaces, with the MAC address, index, MTU and operational state read from
515:  sysfs in the device container (type `veth`, which is how `clabwire` realizes
516:  lab links).
517:  
518: +## Link impairments
519: +
520: +[Impairments in the topology](../impairments.md#declarative-definition)
521: +become the `netem` of the matching endpoint of each c9s Link. On a link between
522: +Pods, the peer Pod's `clabwire` sidecar programs the impairment on its own
523: +sidecar leg, where it receives the endpoint's packets. On same-Pod and host
524: +links, it programs the endpoint's interface instead. It also sets the impairment
525: +again when the interface is recreated, so it survives node restarts without
526: +containerlab.
527: +
528: +In a lab deployed with `--no-topology-cr`, [`tools netem`](../../cmd/tools/netem/set.md)
529: +changes the Link instead of a local network namespace, and `clabwire` applies
530: +the change live, without restarting the node. The change reaches `clabwire`
531: +through a ConfigMap the kubelet syncs into its pod, which can take a minute. It needs `--topo` or `--name`,
532: +and no root privileges:
533: +
534: +```bash
535: +containerlab -r c9s tools netem set -t clos.clab.yml -n srl1 -i e1-1 --delay 50ms --loss 1
536: +containerlab -r c9s tools netem show -t clos.clab.yml
537: +containerlab -r c9s tools netem reset -t clos.clab.yml -n srl1 -i e1-1
538: +```
539: +
540: +`show` lists the impairments the Links declare. A later `deploy` replaces each
541: +Link with the one the topology compiles to, which restores the topology's
542: +impairments, like `start` and `apply` do for local labs. A lab owned by a
543: +Topology resource (the default) rejects `set` and `reset`: the clabernetes
544: +controller renders its Links and reverts any direct change, so its impairments
545: +come from the topology.
546: +
547: +Link impairments need a clabernetes release whose Link has an endpoint
548: +`netem`. containerlab checks the published Link schema the first time a lab
549: +uses them, because an older release would drop the field and deploy the lab
550: +unimpaired. clabernetes programs the delay in 32-bit kernel ticks, so it
551: +accepts delays up to `4m`.
552: +
553:  ## Start, stop, and restart
554:  
555:  Node lifecycle commands ask the clabernetes controllers for a run state; they
556:  never touch Deployments or Pods.
557:

With the [clabernetes runtime](clabernetes/runtime.md#link-impairments), the impairments become part of the lab's Links, and `tools netem` changes them there.
595:

Removing an impairment from the topology, or setting all of its values to zero, doesn't remove it from a running lab; use `tools netem reset` for that.

+\n520: +[Impairments in the topology](../impairments.md#declarative-definition)\n521: +become the `netem` of the matching endpoint of each c9s Link. On a link between\n522: +Pods, the peer Pod's `clabwire` sidecar programs the impairment on its own\n523: +sidecar leg, where it receives the endpoint's packets. On same-Pod and host\n524: +links, it programs the endpoint's interface instead. The change reaches `clabwire`\n531: +through a ConfigMap the kubelet syncs into its pod, which can take a minute. It needs `--topo` or `--name`,\n532: +and no root privileges:\n533: +\n534: +```bash\n535: +containerlab -r c9s tools netem set -t clos.clab.yml -n srl1 -i e1-1 --delay 50ms --loss 1\n536: +containerlab -r c9s tools netem show -t clos.clab.yml\n537: +containerlab -r c9s tools netem reset -t clos.clab.yml -n srl1 -i e1-1\n538: +```\n539: +\n540: +`show` lists the impairments the Links declare. On a link between\n+Pods, the peer Pod's `clabwire` sidecar programs the impairment on its own\n+sidecar leg, where it receives the endpoint's packets. On same-Pod and host\n+links, it programs the endpoint's interface instead. It also sets the impairment\n+again when the interface is recreated, so it survives node restarts without\n+containerlab.\n+\n+In a lab deployed with `--no-topology-cr`, [`tools netem`](../../cmd/tools/netem/set.md)\n+changes the Link instead of a local network namespace, and `clabwire` applies\n+the change live, without restarting the node. The change reaches `clabwire`\n+through a ConfigMap the kubelet syncs into its pod, which can take a minute. It needs `--topo` or `--name`,\n+and no root privileges:\n+\n+```bash\n+containerlab -r c9s tools netem set -t clos.clab.yml -n srl1 -i e1-1 --delay 50ms --loss 1\n+containerlab -r c9s tools netem show -t clos.clab.yml\n+containerlab -r c9s tools netem reset -t clos.clab.yml -n srl1 -i e1-1\n+```\n+\n+`show` lists the impairments the Links declare. A later `deploy` replaces each\n+Link with the one the topology compiles to, which restores the topology's\n+impairments, like `start` and `apply` do for local labs. A lab owned by a\n+Topology resource (the default) rejects `set` and `reset`: the clabernetes\n+controller renders its Links and reverts any direct change, so its impairments\n+come from the topology.\n+\n+Link impairments need a clabernetes release whose Link has an endpoint\n+`netem`. containerlab checks the published Link schema the first time a lab\n+uses them, because an older release would drop the field and deploy the lab\n+unimpaired. clabernetes programs the delay in 32-bit kernel ticks, so it\n+accepts delays up to `4m`.\n+\n ## Start, stop, and restart\n \n Node lifecycle commands ask the clabernetes controllers for a run state; they\n never touch Deployments or Pods.\n \n@@ -1413,19 +1448,18 @@ Known command differences:\n - Destroy flags `--graceful` and `--keep-mgmt-net` are rejected. `--cleanup`\n   also deletes the lab's persistent claims (saved device state) and removes\n   the local lab directory; a plain destroy keeps the claims.\n - Local Docker commands on the outer host are not authoritative for c9s labs.\n - `inspect interfaces` lists only the lab link interfaces (those `capture`\n-  accepts), not the management or pod interfaces. Host-side `tc` or netem\n-  operations do not have the same local namespace access they have with Docker\n-  labs.\n+  accepts), not the management or pod interfaces.\n - `graph` renders from the topology file only: `--mermaid`, `--dot`, `--drawio`\n   and `--offline` work, the default mode that reads running containers is\n   rejected, and so is `--node-filter`. `--drawio` runs the clab-io-draw\n   container, so it needs Docker or Podman on the outer host.\n - `tools` commands operate on local containers and host networking and are\n-  rejected with an error when the `c9s` runtime is selected.\n+  rejected with an error when the `c9s` runtime is selected, except\n+  [`tools netem`](#link-impairments), which changes the lab's Links.\n - Per-node `runtime: docker` or `runtime: podman` is not the same as selecting\n   the global `c9s` lab runtime.\n - A lab name maps to one canonical `c9s-<lab-name>` namespace in the selected\n   cluster.\n - c9s 0.9 removed `Topology.spec.naming`. 989: +	}
990: +
991: +	patch, err := json.Marshal(map[string]any{
992: +		"spec": map[string]any{endpoint: map[string]any{"netem": netem}},
993: +	})
994: +	if err != nil {
995: +		return err
996: +	}
997: +
998: +	_, err = r.client.Resource(linkGVR).Namespace(location.Namespace).Patch(
999: +		ctx, link.GetName(), types.MergePatchType, patch, metav1.PatchOptions{},
1000: +	)
1001: +	if err != nil {
1002: +		return fmt.Errorf("failed to set the impairment of c9s link %s/%s: %w",
1003: +			location.Namespace, link.GetName(), err)
1004: +	}
1005: +
1006: +	return nil
1007: +}
1008: +
1009: +// Impairments lists the impaired link interfaces of the requested nodes, or of every node, as
1010: +// their c9s Links declare them.
1011: +func (r *Runtime) Impairments(
1012: +	ctx context.Context,
1013: +	req clablabruntime.NodeRequest,
1014: +) ([]clablabruntime.NodeImpairments, error) {
1015: +	r, err := r.connect(ctx, req.Identity)
1016: +	if err != nil {
1017: +		return nil, err
1018: +	}
1019: +
1020: +	locations, err := r.LocateNode(ctx, req)
1021: +	if err != nil || len(locations) == 0 {
1022: +		return nil, err
1023: +	}
1024: +
1025: +	names, err := r.nodeDisplayNames(ctx, req.Name, locations)
1026: +	if err != nil {
1027: +		return nil, err
1028: +	}
1029: +
1030: +	links, err := r.client.Resource(linkGVR).Namespace(locations[0].Namespace).List(
1031: +		ctx,
1032: +		metav1.ListOptions{LabelSelector: labels.Set{labelTopologyOwner: req.Name}.String()},
1033: +	)
1034: +	if err != nil {
1035: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to list c9s links for lab %s/%s: %w",
1036: +			locations[0].Namespace, req.Name, err)
1037: +	}
1038: +
1039: +	impairments := map[string][]clabtypes.ImpairmentData{}
1040: +	for _, location := range locations {
1041: +		impairments[location.NodeName] = nil
1042: +	}
1043: +
1044: +	for idx := range links.Items {
1045: +		for _, endpoint := range linkEndpointFields {
1046: +			node, _, _ := unstructured.NestedString(links.Items[idx].Object,
1047: +				"spec", endpoint, "nodeName")
1048: +			iface, _, _ := unstructured.NestedString(links.Items[idx].Object,
1049: +				"spec", endpoint, "interfaceName")
1050: +			netem, found, _ := unstructured.NestedMap(links.Items[idx].Object,
1051: +				"spec", endpoint, "netem")
1052: +
1053: +			if _, requested := impairments[node]; !requested || !found || len(netem) == 0 {
1054: +				continue
1055: +			}
1056: +
1057: +			impairments[node] = append(impairments[node], impairmentData(iface, netem))
1058: +		}
1059: +	}
1060: +
1061: +	result := make([]clablabruntime.NodeImpairments, 0, len(locations))
1062: +	for _, location := range locations {
1063: +		nodeImpairments := impairments[location.NodeName]
1064: +		sort.Slice(nodeImpairments, func(i, j int) bool {
1065: +			return nodeImpairments[i].Interface < nodeImpairments[j].Interface
1066: +		})
1067: +
1068: +		result = append(result, clablabruntime.NodeImpairments{
1069: +			Node:        names.display(location.NodeName),
1070: +			Impairments: nodeImpairments,
1071: +		})
1072: +	}
1073: +
1074: +	sort.Slice(result, func(i, j int) bool { return result[i].Node < result[j].Node })
1075: +
1076: +	return result, nil
1077: +}
1078: +
1079: +// linksDeclareNetem reports whether any of the Links impairs one of its endpoints.
1080: +func linksDeclareNetem(links []*unstructured.Unstructured) bool {
1081: +	for _, link := range links {
1082: +		for _, endpoint := range linkEndpointFields {
1083: +			if _, found, _ := unstructured.NestedFieldNoCopy(link.Object,
1084: +				"spec", endpoint, "netem"); found {
1085: +				return true
1086: +			}
1087: +		}
1088: +	}
1089: +
1090: +	return false
1091: +}
1092: +
1093: +// linkEndpoint finds the c9s Link with an endpoint on the node's interface and returns it with
1094: +// the spec field of that endpoint.
1095: +func linkEndpoint(
1096: +	links []unstructured.Unstructured,
1097: +	node,
1098: +	iface string,
1099: +) (*unstructured.Unstructured, string, bool) {
1100: +	for idx := range links {
1101: +		for _, endpoint := range linkEndpointFields {
1102: +			endpointNode, _, _ := unstructured.NestedString(links[idx].Object,
1103: +				"spec", endpoint, "nodeName")
1104: +			endpointIface, _, _ := unstructured.NestedString(links[idx].Object,
1105: +				"spec", endpoint, "interfaceName")
1106: +
1107: +			if endpointNode == node && endpointIface == iface {
1108: +				return &links[idx], endpoint, true
1109: +			}
1110: +		}
1111: +	}
1112: +
1113: +	return nil, "", false
1114: +}
1115: +
1116: +// linkNetem renders an impairment in the c9s Link vocabulary, which is containerlab's.
1117: +func linkNetem(impairment *clablabruntime.Impairment) map[string]any {
1118: +	netem := map[string]any{}
1119: +
1120: +	if impairment.Delay != 0 {
1121: +		netem["delay"] = impairment.Delay.String()
1122: +	}
1123: +	if impairment.Jitter != 0 {
1124: +		netem["jitter"] = impairment.Jitter.String()
1125: +	}
1126: +	if impairment.Loss != 0 {
1127: +		netem["loss"] = impairment.Loss
1128: +	}
1129: +	if impairment.Rate != 0 {
1130: +		netem["rate"] = impairment.Rate
1131: +	}
1132: +	if impairment.Corruption != 0 {
1133: +		netem["corruption"] = impairment.Corruption
1134: +	}
1135: +
1136: +	return netem
1137: +}
1138: +
1139: +// impairmentData converts a c9s Link endpoint netem into the shape tools netem show reports for
1140: +// local labs.
1141: +func impairmentData(iface string, netem map[string]any) clabtypes.ImpairmentData {
1142: +	data := clabtypes.ImpairmentData{Interface: iface}
1143: +
1144: +	if delay, ok := netem["delay"].(string); ok {
1145: +		data.Delay = normalizedDuration(delay)
1146: +	}
1147: +	if jitter, ok := netem["jitter"].(string); ok {
1148: +		data.Jitter = normalizedDuration(jitter)
1149: +	}
1150: +
1151: +	data.PacketLoss = roundedPercent(netem["loss"])
1152: +	data.Corruption = roundedPercent(netem["corruption"])
1153: +
1154: +	switch rate := netem["rate"].(type) {
1155: +	case int64:
1156: +		data.Rate = int(rate)
1157: +	case float64:
1158: +		data.Rate = int(rate)
1159: +	}
1160: +
1161: +	return data
1162: +}
1163: +
1164: +func normalizedDuration(value string) string {
1165: +	duration, err := time.ParseDuration(value)
1166: +	if err != nil {
1167: +		return value
1168: +	}
1169: +
1170: +	return duration.String()
1171: +}
1172: +
1173: +// roundedPercent rounds a percentage to 2 decimal places, like tools netem show.
1174: +func roundedPercent(value any) float64 {
1175: +	var percent float64
1176: +
1177: +	switch typed := value.(type) {
1178: +	case int64:
1179: +		percent = float64(typed)
1180: +	case float64:
1181: +		percent = typed
1182: +	}
1183: +
1184: +	return math.Round(percent*100) / 100 //nolint:mnd
1185: +}

1925: index 0000000..033e867
1926: --- /dev/null
1927: +++ b/tests/14-clabernetes/03-link-netem.robot
1928: @@ -0,0 +1,103 @@
1929: +*** Comments ***
1930: +This suite tests link impairments with the c9s runtime: the topology's impairments become the
1931: +netem of the c9s Links and clabwire programs them on the receiving sidecar legs, and tools netem
1932: +changes the Links of a lab deployed with --no-topology-cr.
1933: +
1934: +
1935: +*** Settings ***
1936: +Library             OperatingSystem
1937: +Library             Process
1938: +Library             String
1939: +Resource            ../common.robot
1940: +
1941: +Suite Setup         Setup
1942: +Suite Teardown      Run Clab Command    destroy -t ${topo} --cleanup
1943: +Test Tags           clabernetes    c9s
1944: +
1945: +
1946: +*** Variables ***
1947: +${runtime}          c9s
1948: +${lab-name}         c9s-link-netem
1949: +${topo}             ${CURDIR}/03-link-netem.clab.yml
1950: +${lab-namespace}    c9s-${lab-name}
1951: +${server-label}     clab-node-name\=server
1952: +
1953: +
1954: +*** Test Cases ***
1955: +Deploy c9s lab with link impairments
1956: +    ${output} =    Run Clab Command    deploy -t ${topo}
1957: +    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${output.rc}    0
1958: +
1959: +The Link declares the topology's impairment
1960: +    ${links} =    Process.Run Process
1961: +    ...    kubectl -n ${lab-namespace} get links.c9s.run -l c9s.run/topologyOwner\=${lab-name} -o jsonpath\='{.items[*].spec.endpointA.netem.delay}'
1962: +    ...    shell=True
1963: +    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${links.rc}    0
1964: +    Should Be Equal    ${links.stdout}    50ms
1965: +
1966: +Clabwire programs the impairment on the receiving sidecar leg
1967: +    Wait Until Keyword Succeeds    120s    5s    Server Sidecar Qdisc Should Contain    delay 50ms
1968: +
1969: +Tools netem shows the impairment
1970: +    ${output} =    Run Clab Command    tools netem show -t ${topo} -n client -f json
1971: +    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${output.rc}    0
1972: +    Should Contain    ${output.stdout}    "delay": "50ms"
1973: +
1974: +Tools netem leaves a Topology-owned lab to the topology
1975: +    ${output} =    Run Clab Command    tools netem set -t ${topo} -n client -i eth1 --delay 200ms
1976: +    Should Not Be Equal As Integers    ${output.rc}    0
1977: +    Should Contain    ${output.stderr}    --no-topology-cr
1978: +
1979: +Deploy the lab without a Topology resource
1980: +    ${output} =    Run Clab Command    destroy -t ${topo} --cleanup
1981: +    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${output.rc}    0
1982: +    ${output} =    Run Clab Command    deploy -t ${topo} --no-topology-cr
1983: +    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${output.rc}    0
1984: +    Wait Until Keyword Succeeds    120s    5s    Server Sidecar Qdisc Should Contain    delay 50ms
1985: +
1986: +Tools netem changes the impairment live
1987: +    ${output} =    Run Clab Command    tools netem set -t ${topo} -n client -i eth1 --delay 200ms --loss 1
1988: +    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${output.rc}    0
1989: +    Should Contain    ${output.stdout}    200ms
1990: +    Wait Until Keyword Succeeds    180s    5s    Server Sidecar Qdisc Should Contain    delay 200ms
1991: +
1992: +Tools netem resets the impairment
1993: +    ${output} =    Run Clab Command    tools netem reset -t ${topo} -n client -i eth1
1994: +    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${output.rc}    0
1995: +    Wait Until Keyword Succeeds    180s    5s    Server Sidecar Should Have No Impairment
1996: +
1997: +A deploy restores the topology's impairments
1998: +    ${output} =    Run Clab Command    deploy -t ${topo} --no-topology-cr
1999: +    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${output.rc}    0
2000: +    Wait Until Keyword Succeeds    180s    5s    Server Sidecar Qdisc Should Contain    delay 50ms
2001: +
2002: +
2003: +*** Keywords ***
2004: +Setup
2005: +    Skip If    '${runtime}' != 'c9s'    This suite targets the c9s runtime.
2006: +    ${output} =    Run Clab Command    destroy -t ${topo} --cleanup
2007: +    Log    Cleanup return code: ${output.rc}
2008: +
2009: +Run Clab Command
2010: +    [Arguments]    ${args}
2011: +    ${output} =    Process.Run Process
2012: +    ...    ${CLAB_BIN} --runtime ${runtime} ${args}
2013: +    ...    shell=True
2014: +    Log    stdout:${\n}${output.stdout}    console=${True}
2015: +    Log    stderr:${\n}${output.stderr}    console=${True}
2016: +    RETURN    ${output}
2017: +
2018: +Server Sidecar Qdisc Should Contain
2019: +    [Arguments]    ${expected}
2020: +    ${output} =    Server Sidecar Qdiscs
2021: +    Should Contain    ${output.stdout}${output.stderr}    ${expected}
2022: +
2023: +Server Sidecar Should Have No Impairment
2024: +    ${output} =    Server Sidecar Qdiscs
2025: +    Should Not Contain    ${output.stdout}${output.stderr}    netem c9:
2026: +
2027: +Server Sidecar Qdiscs
2028: +    ${output} =    Run Clab Command
2029: +    ...    exec -t ${topo} --label ${server-label} --cmd 'tc qdisc show'
2030: +    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${output.rc}    0
2031: +    RETURN    ${output}

(End of file - total 2031 lines)

404: func (r *Runtime) deployTopology(
405: 	ctx context.Context,
406: 	req clablabruntime.DeployRequest,
407: 	namespace string,
408: 	prepared *preparedDeployment,
409: 	primitiveExists bool,
410: ) (*clablabruntime.LabState, error) {
411: 	stagedConfigMaps := prepared.configMaps
412: 
413: 	managedNamespace := req.Namespace == "" && r.labNamespaceOverride == ""
414: 	namespaceCreated, err := r.ensureLabNamespace(ctx, req.Name, namespace, managedNamespace)
415: 	if err != nil {
416: 		return nil, err
417: 	}
418: 	// A fresh deployment is transactional: a failure removes only what this operation created.
419: 	// Once the controller has adopted pre-existing primitive resources, deleting the Topology
420: 	// would cascade to them, so an existing lab is always retained for diagnosis and recovery.
421: 	//
422: 	// The rollback only deletes the Topology while it is still the one this operation created:
423: 	// a concurrent deploy reconciles the same Topology in place, and deleting it there would
424: 	// cascade to the lab the newer deploy put in place.
425: 	var createdTopology *unstructured.Unstructured
426: 
427: 	cleanupFresh := func(topologyCreated bool) {
428: 		if primitiveExists {
429: 			return
430: 		}
431: 		if topologyCreated &&
432: 			r.topologyChangedSinceCreate(ctx, namespace, req.Name, createdTopology) {
433: 			log.FromContext(ctx).Info(
434: 				"leaving the C9s lab in place: its Topology changed since this deploy started",
435: 				"name", req.Name,
436: 				"namespace", namespace,
437: 			)
438: 
439: 			return
440: 		}
441: 		if topologyCreated {
442: 			_ = r.client.Resource(topologyGVR).Namespace(namespace).
443: 				Delete(ctx, req.Name, metav1.DeleteOptions{})
444: 		}
445: 		r.deleteStagedConfigMaps(ctx, namespace, stagedConfigMaps)
446: 		if namespaceCreated {
447: 			_, _ = r.deleteManagedLabNamespace(ctx, req.Name, namespace)
448: 		}
449: 	}
450: 
451: 	if err = r.applyStagedConfigMaps(
452: 		ctx,
453: 		namespace,
454: 		req.Name,
455: 		stagedConfigMaps,
456: 		req.MaxWorkers,
457: 	); err != nil {
458: 		if namespaceCreated {
459: 			_, _ = r.deleteManagedLabNamespace(ctx, req.Name, namespace)
460: 		}
461: 
462: 		return nil, err
463: 	}
464: 
465: 	operation := "Creating"
466: 	if primitiveExists {
467: 		operation = "Adopting"
468: 	}
469: 	log.FromContext(ctx).Info(
470: 		operation+" C9s lab topology",
471: 		"name", req.Name,
472: 		"namespace", namespace,
473: 		"nodes", len(prepared.primitives.nodes),
474: 		"links", len(prepared.primitives.links),
475: 	)
476: 	created, err := r.client.Resource(topologyGVR).Namespace(namespace).
477: 		Create(ctx, prepared.topology.DeepCopy(), metav1.CreateOptions{})
478: 	if err != nil {
479: 		cleanupFresh(false)
480: 
481: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create clabernetes topology %s/%s: %w",
482: 			namespace, req.Name, err)
483: 	}
484: 	createdTopology = created
485: 
486: 	if !req.Wait {
487: 		return r.Inspect(ctx, clablabruntime.InspectRequest{Name: req.Name, Namespace: namespace})
488: 	}
489: 
490: 	if err = r.awaitTopologyConverged(ctx, req, namespace, prepared.configMaps); err != nil {
491: 		cleanupFresh(true)
492: 
493: 		return nil, err
494: 	}
495: 
496: 	return r.Inspect(ctx, clablabruntime.InspectRequest{Name: req.Name, Namespace: namespace})
497: }
498: 
499: // topologyChangedSinceCreate reports whether the stored Topology no longer matches the one
500: // this deploy created. A mismatch means another writer changed the lab definition while this
501: // deploy was waiting; the rollback then belongs to the newer deploy and must not cascade to it.
502: func (r *Runtime) topologyChangedSinceCreate(
503: 	ctx context.Context,
504: 	namespace,
505: 	name string,
506: 	created *unstructured.Unstructured,
507: ) bool {
508: 	topology, err := r.client.Resource(topologyGVR).Namespace(namespace).
509: 		Get(ctx, name, metav1.GetOptions{})
510: 	if err != nil {
511: 		// The Topology is gone or unreadable, so deleting it cannot cascade to anyone;
512: 		// the staged artifacts and the managed namespace can still be cleaned up.
513: 		return false
514: 	}
515: 
516: 	// The UID guards against a delete-and-recreate reusing the name for a different lab,
517: 	// and the generation against an in-place reconcile that did not change the spec.
518: 	if topology.GetUID() != created.GetUID() ||
519: 		topology.GetGeneration() != created.GetGeneration() {
520: 		return true
521: 	}
522: 
523: 	// The spec comparison detects a concurrent deploy whose update replaced the definition.
524: 	// It reuses the same equivalence the reconcile path relies on to treat API defaulting
525: 	// as a no-op.
526: 	return !apiequality.Semantic.DeepEqual(
527: 		normalizeAPIDefaultedJSON(topology.Object["spec"]),
528: 		normalizeAPIDefaultedJSON(created.Object["spec"]),
529: 	)
530: }
531: 
532: // reconcileTopology updates the definition of an existing Topology-owned lab in place and waits
533: // for the controller to converge the compiled primitive resources on it.
534: func (r *Runtime) reconcileTopology(
535: 	ctx context.Context,
536: 	req clablabruntime.DeployRequest,
537: 	namespace string,
538: 	prepared *preparedDeployment,
539: ) (*clablabruntime.LabState, error) {
540: 	desired := prepared.topology
541: 	stagedConfigMaps := prepared.configMaps
542: 
543: 	if err := r.applyStagedConfigMaps(
544: 		ctx,
545: 		namespace,
546: 		req.Name,
547: 		stagedConfigMaps,
548: 		req.MaxWorkers,
549: 	); err != nil {
550: 		return nil, err
551: 	}
552: 
553: 	resource := r.client.Resource(topologyGVR).Namespace(namespace)
554: 	err := retry.RetryOnConflict(retry.DefaultRetry, func() error {
555: 		latest, err := resource.Get(ctx, req.Name, metav1.GetOptions{})
556: 		if err != nil {
557: 			return err
558: 		}
559: 
560: 		// The Topology naming field is immutable and required once set; carry the stored value
561: 		// forward so replacing the spec cannot strip it.
562: 		if naming, found, _ := unstructured.NestedString(
563: 			latest.Object, "spec", "naming",
564: 		); found && naming != "" {
565: 			desired = desired.DeepCopy()
566: 			if err := unstructured.SetNestedField(
567: 				desired.Object, naming, "spec", "naming",
568: 			); err != nil {
569: 				return err
570: 			}
571: 		}
572: 
573: 		updated := reconciledPrimitiveObject(latest, desired)
574: 		if primitiveObjectsConform(latest, updated) {
575: 			return nil
576: 		}
577: 
578: 		_, err = resource.Update(ctx, updated, metav1.UpdateOptions{})
579: 		return err
580: 	})
581: 	if err != nil {
582: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to reconcile clabernetes topology %s/%s: %w",
583: 			namespace, req.Name, err)
584: 	}
585: 
586: 	if !req.Wait {
587: 		return r.Inspect(ctx, clablabruntime.InspectRequest{Name: req.Name, Namespace: namespace})
588: 	}
589: 	if err := r.awaitTopologyConverged(ctx, req, namespace, prepared.configMaps); err != nil {
590: 		return nil, err
591: 	}
592: 
593: 	return r.Inspect(ctx, clablabruntime.InspectRequest{Name: req.Name, Namespace: namespace})

23: // SetImpairment sets the netem impairment of one lab link interface on the endpoint of its c9s
24: // Link, or removes it when the request carries none. The connectivity sidecar of the node's pod
25: // applies the change live; a later deploy restores the impairments the topology declares. A lab
26: // owned by a Topology resource is rejected: its controller renders the Links and reverts any
27: // direct change, so its impairments come from the topology.
28: func (r *Runtime) SetImpairment(
29: 	ctx context.Context,
30: 	req clablabruntime.ImpairmentRequest,
31: ) error {
32: 	r, err := r.connect(ctx, req.Identity)
33: 	if err != nil {
34: 		return err
35: 	}
36: 
37: 	if err = r.ensureLinkNetemSupport(ctx); err != nil {
38: 		return err
39: 	}
40: 
41: 	locations, err := r.LocateNode(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{
42: 		Name: req.Name, Namespace: req.Namespace, Nodes: []string{req.Node},
43: 		Identity: req.Identity,
44: 	})
45: 	if err != nil {
46: 		return err
47: 	}
48: 	location := locations[0]
49: 
50: 	_, err = r.client.Resource(topologyGVR).Namespace(location.Namespace).
51: 		Get(ctx, req.Name, metav1.GetOptions{})
52: 	switch {
53: 	case err == nil:
54: 		return fmt.Errorf("c9s lab %s/%s is owned by a Topology resource, whose controller "+
55: 			"reverts changes to its links; declare the impairment in the topology and deploy "+
56: 			"again, or deploy the lab with --no-topology-cr", location.Namespace, req.Name)
57: 	case !apierrors.IsNotFound(err):
58: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get clabernetes topology %s/%s: %w",
59: 			location.Namespace, req.Name, err)
60: 	}
61: 
62: 	links, err := r.primitiveResourcesForTopology(ctx, linkGVR, req.Name, location.Namespace)
63: 	if err != nil {
64: 		return err
65: 	}
66: 
67: 	link, endpoint, ok := linkEndpoint(links.Items, location.NodeName, req.Interface)
68: 	if !ok {
69: 		return fmt.Errorf("interface %q of node %q is not on a link of c9s lab %s/%s",
70: 			req.Interface, req.Node, location.Namespace, req.Name)
71: 	}
72: 
73: 	// a merge patch with a null netem removes it
74: 	var netem any
75: 	if req.Impairment != nil {
76: 		netem = linkNetem(req.Impairment)
77: 	}
78: 
79: 	patch, err := json.Marshal(map[string]any{
80: 		"spec": map[string]any{endpoint: map[string]any{"netem": netem}},
81: 	})
82: 	if err != nil {
83: 		return err
84: 	}
85: 
86: 	_, err = r.client.Resource(linkGVR).Namespace(location.Namespace).Patch(
87: 		ctx, link.GetName(), types.MergePatchType, patch, metav1.PatchOptions{},
88: 	)
89: 	if err != nil {
90: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to set the impairment of c9s link %s/%s: %w",
91: 			location.Namespace, link.GetName(), err)
92: 	}
93: 
94: 	return nil
95: }

97: // Impairments lists the impaired link interfaces of the requested nodes, or of every node, as
98: // their c9s Links declare them.
99: func (r *Runtime) Impairments(
100: 	ctx context.Context,
101: 	req clablabruntime.NodeRequest,
102: ) ([]clablabruntime.NodeImpairments, error) {
103: 	r, err := r.connect(ctx, req.Identity)
104: 	if err != nil {
105: 		return nil, err
106: 	}
107: 
108: 	locations, err := r.LocateNode(ctx, req)
109: 	if err != nil || len(locations) == 0 {
110: 		return nil, err
111: 	}
112: 
113: 	names, err := r.nodeDisplayNames(ctx, req.Name, locations)
114: 	if err != nil {
115: 		return nil, err
116: 	}
117: 
118: 	links, err := r.client.Resource(linkGVR).Namespace(locations[0].Namespace).List(
119: 		ctx,
120: 		metav1.ListOptions{LabelSelector: labels.Set{labelTopologyOwner: req.Name}.String()},
121: 	)
122: 	if err != nil {
123: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to list c9s links for lab %s/%s: %w",
124: 			locations[0].Namespace, req.Name, err)
125: 	}
126: 
127: 	impairments := map[string][]clabtypes.ImpairmentData{}
128: 	for _, location := range locations {
129: 		impairments[location.NodeName] = nil
130: 	}
131: 
132: 	for idx := range links.Items {
133: 		for _, endpoint := range linkEndpointFields {
134: 			node, _, _ := unstructured.NestedString(links.Items[idx].Object,
135: 				"spec", endpoint, "nodeName")
136: 			iface, _, _ := unstructured.NestedString(links.Items[idx].Object,
137: 				"spec", endpoint, "interfaceName")
138: 			netem, found, _ := unstructured.NestedMap(links.Items[idx].Object,
139: 				"spec", endpoint, "netem")
140: 
141: 			if _, requested := impairments[node]; !requested || !found || len(netem) == 0 {
142: 				continue
143: 			}
144: 
145: 			impairments[node] = append(impairments[node], impairmentData(iface, netem))
146: 		}
147: 	}
148: 
149: 	result := make([]clablabruntime.NodeImpairments, 0, len(locations))
150: 	for _, location := range locations {
151: 		nodeImpairments := impairments[location.NodeName]
152: 		sort.Slice(nodeImpairments, func(i, j int) bool {
153: 			return nodeImpairments[i].Interface < nodeImpairments[j].Interface
154: 		})
155: 
156: 		result = append(result, clablabruntime.NodeImpairments{
157: 			Node:        names.display(location.NodeName),
158: 			Impairments: nodeImpairments,
159: 		})
160: 	}
161: 
162: 	sort.Slice(result, func(i, j int) bool { return result[i].Node < result[j].Node })
163: 
164: 	return result, nil
165: }

167: // linksDeclareNetem reports whether any of the Links impairs one of its endpoints.
168: func linksDeclareNetem(links []*unstructured.Unstructured) bool {
169: 	for _, link := range links {
170: 		for _, endpoint := range linkEndpointFields {
171: 			if _, found, _ := unstructured.NestedFieldNoCopy(link.Object,
172: 				"spec", endpoint, "netem"); found {
173: 				return true
174: 			}
175: 		}
176: 	}
177: 
178: 	return false
179: }
180: 
181: // linkEndpoint finds the c9s Link with an endpoint on the node's interface and returns it with
182: // the spec field of that endpoint.
183: func linkEndpoint(
184: 	links []unstructured.Unstructured,
185: 	node,
186: 	iface string,
187: ) (*unstructured.Unstructured, string, bool) {
188: 	for idx := range links {
189: 		for _, endpoint := range linkEndpointFields {
190: 			endpointNode, _, _ := unstructured.NestedString(links[idx].Object,
191: 				"spec", endpoint, "nodeName")
192: 			endpointIface, _, _ := unstructured.NestedString(links[idx].Object,
193: 				"spec", endpoint, "interfaceName")
194: 
195: 			if endpointNode == node && endpointIface == iface {
196: 				return &links[idx], endpoint, true
197: 			}
198: 		}
199: 	}
200: 
201: 	return nil, "", false
202: }
203: 
204: // linkNetem renders an impairment in the c9s Link vocabulary, which is containerlab's.
205: func linkNetem(impairment *clablabruntime.Impairment) map[string]any {
206: 	netem := map[string]any{}
207: 
208: 	if impairment.Delay != 0 {
209: 		netem["delay"] = impairment.Delay.String()
210: 	}
211: 	if impairment.Jitter != 0 {
212: 		netem["jitter"] = impairment.Jitter.String()
213: 	}
214: 	if impairment.Loss != 0 {
215: 		netem["loss"] = impairment.Loss
216: 	}
217: 	if impairment.Rate != 0 {
218: 		netem["rate"] = impairment.Rate
219: 	}
220: 	if impairment.Corruption != 0 {
221: 		netem["corruption"] = impairment.Corruption
222: 	}
223: 
224: 	return netem
225: }
226: 
227: // impairmentData converts a c9s Link endpoint netem into the shape tools netem show reports for
228: // local labs.
229: func impairmentData(iface string, netem map[string]any) clabtypes.ImpairmentData {
230: 	data := clabtypes.ImpairmentData{Interface: iface}
231: 
232: 	if delay, ok := netem["delay"].(string); ok {
233: 		data.Delay = normalizedDuration(delay)
234: 	}
235: 	if jitter, ok := netem["jitter"].(string); ok {
236: 		data.Jitter = normalizedDuration(jitter)
237: 	}
238: 
239: 	data.PacketLoss = roundedPercent(netem["loss"])
240: 	data.Corruption = roundedPercent(netem["corruption"])
241: 
242: 	switch rate := netem["rate"].(type) {
243: 	case int64:
244: 		data.Rate = int(rate)
245: 	case float64:
246: 		data.Rate = int(rate)
247: 	}
248: 
249: 	return data
250: }
251: 
252: func normalizedDuration(value string) string {
253: 	duration, err := time.ParseDuration(value)
254: 	if err != nil {
255: 		return value
256: 	}
257: 
258: 	return duration.String()
259: }
260: 
261: // roundedPercent rounds a percentage to 2 decimal places, like tools netem show.
262: func roundedPercent(value any) float64 {
263: 	var percent float64
264: 
265: 	switch typed := value.(type) {
266: 	case int64:
267: 		percent = float64(typed)
268: 	case float64:
269: 		percent = typed
270: 	}
271: 
272: 	return math.Round(percent*100) / 100 //nolint:mnd
273: }

It is skipped when the clients were injected (tests).\nfunc (r *Runtime) ensureLinkNetemSupport(ctx context.Context) error {\n\treturn r.netemSupport.ensure(ctx, r)\n}\n\n// resolveOpenAPIProperty returns a property of a schema, following $ref and allOf.\nfunc resolveOpenAPIProperty(\n\tdoc openAPIDocument,\n\tschema openAPISchema,\n\tname string,\n) (openAPISchema, bool) {\n\tfor range 8 {\n\t\tif property, ok := schema.Properties[name]; ok {\n\t\t\treturn resolveOpenAPIRef(doc, property), true\n\t\t}\n\t\tswitch {\n\t\tcase schema.Ref != \"\":\n\t\t\tschema = resolveOpenAPIRef(doc, schema)\n\t\tcase len(schema.AllOf) == 1:\n\t\t\tschema = resolveOpenAPIRef(doc, schema.AllOf[0])\n\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\treturn openAPISchema{}, false\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn openAPISchema{}, false\n}\n\nfunc resolveOpenAPIRef(doc openAPIDocument, schema openAPISchema) openAPISchema {\n\tfor range 8 {\n\t\tswitch {\n\t\tcase schema.Ref != \"\":\n\t\t\tname := strings.TrimPrefix(schema.Ref, \"#/components/schemas/\")\n\t\t\tresolved, ok := doc.Components.Schemas[name]\n\t\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\t\treturn schema\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tschema = resolved\n\t\tcase len(schema.AllOf) == 1 && len(schema.Properties) == 0:\n\t\t\tschema = schema.AllOf[0]\n\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\treturn schema\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn schema\n}\n\n// CheckSupport checks that the cluster runs a clabernetes release with the contract the c9s\n// runtime needs, and returns an error wrapping labruntime.ErrUnsupportedRuntimeVersion that\n// names the required release when it does not. Every cluster operation runs the same check\n// once per runtime instance; servers call it at startup to fail early.\nfunc (r *Runtime) CheckSupport(ctx context.Context, identity clablabruntime.Identity) error {\n\t_, err := r.connect(ctx, identity)\n\n\treturn err\n}",

510: --- a/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md
511: +++ b/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md
512: @@ -701,10 +701,45 @@ Capturing needs `get` and `create` on `pods/exec` in the lab namespace, which
513:  `clabernetes-lab-editor` grants. `inspect interfaces -r c9s` lists the same
514:  interfaces, with the MAC address, index, MTU and operational state read from
515:  sysfs in the device container (type `veth`, which is how `clabwire` realizes
516:  lab links).
517:  
518: +## Link impairments
519: +
520: +[Impairments in the topology](../impairments.md#declarative-definition)
521: +become the `netem` of the matching endpoint of each c9s Link. On a link between
522: +Pods, the peer Pod's `clabwire` sidecar programs the impairment on its own
523: +sidecar leg, where it receives the endpoint's packets. On same-Pod and host
524: +links, it programs the endpoint's interface instead. It also sets the impairment
525: +again when the interface is recreated, so it survives node restarts without
526: +containerlab.
527: +
528: +In a lab deployed with `--no-topology-cr`, [`tools netem`](../../cmd/tools/netem/set.md)
529: +changes the Link instead of a local network namespace, and `clabwire` applies
530: +the change live, without restarting the node. The change reaches `clabwire`
531: +through a ConfigMap the kubelet syncs into its pod, which can take a minute. It needs `--topo` or `--name`,
532: +and no root privileges:
533: +
534: +```bash
535: +containerlab -r c9s tools netem set -t clos.clab.yml -n srl1 -i e1-1 --delay 50ms --loss 1
536: +containerlab -r c9s tools netem show -t clos.clab.yml
537: +containerlab -r c9s tools netem reset -t clos.clab.yml -n srl1 -i e1-1
538: +```
539: +
540: +`show` lists the impairments the Links declare. A later `deploy` replaces each
541: +Link with the one the topology compiles to, which restores the topology's
542: +impairments, like `start` and `apply` do for local labs. A lab owned by a
543: +Topology resource (the default) rejects `set` and `reset`: the clabernetes
544: +controller renders its Links and reverts any direct change, so its impairments
545: +come from the topology.
546: +
547: +Link impairments need a clabernetes release whose Link has an endpoint
548: +`netem`. containerlab checks the published Link schema the first time a lab
549: +uses them, because an older release would drop the field and deploy the lab
550: +unimpaired. clabernetes programs the delay in 32-bit kernel ticks, so it
551: +accepts delays up to `4m`.
552: +
553:  ## Start, stop, and restart
554:  
555:  Node lifecycle commands ask the clabernetes controllers for a run state; they
556:  never touch Deployments or Pods.

On SR-SIM endpoints of extended `veth` links they have no effect either, and containerlab warns about it. With the [clabernetes runtime](clabernetes/runtime.md#link-impairments), the impairments become part of the lab's Links, and `tools netem` changes them there.
595:

        "text": "diff --git a/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md b/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md\nindex 3a959ea..bd1e07e 100644\n--- a/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md\n+++ b/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md\n@@ -701,10 +701,45 @@ Capturing needs `get` and `create` on `pods/exec` in the lab namespace, which\n `clabernetes-lab-editor` grants. `inspect interfaces -r c9s` lists the same\n interfaces, with the MAC address, index, MTU and operational state read from\n sysfs in the device container (type `veth`, which is how `clabwire` realizes\n lab links).\n \n+## Link impairments\n+\n+[Impairments in the topology](../impairments.md#declarative-definition)\n+become the `netem` of the matching endpoint of each c9s Link. On a link between\n+Pods, the peer Pod's `clabwire` sidecar programs the impairment on its own\n+sidecar leg, where it receives the endpoint's packets. On same-Pod and host\n+links, it programs the endpoint's interface instead. It also sets the impairment\n+again when the interface is recreated, so it survives node restarts without\n+containerlab.\n+\n+In a lab deployed with `--no-topology-cr`, [`tools netem`](../../cmd/tools/netem/set.md)\n+changes the Link instead of a local network namespace, and `clabwire` applies\n+the change live, without restarting the node. The change reaches `clabwire`\n+through a ConfigMap the kubelet syncs into its pod, which can take a minute. It needs `--topo` or `--name`,\n+and no root privileges:\n+\n+```bash\n+containerlab -r c9s tools netem set -t clos.clab.yml -n srl1 -i e1-1 --delay 50ms --loss 1\n+containerlab -r c9s tools netem show -t clos.clab.yml\n+containerlab -r c9s tools netem reset -t clos.clab.yml -n srl1 -i e1-1\n+```\n+\n+`show` lists the impairments the Links declare. A later `deploy` replaces each\n+Link with the one the topology compiles to, which restores the topology's\n+impairments, like `start` and `apply` do for local labs. A lab owned by a\n+Topology resource (the default) rejects `set` and `reset`: the clabernetes\n+controller renders its Links and reverts any direct change, so its impairments\n+come from the topology.\n+\n+Link impairments need a clabernetes release whose Link has an endpoint\n+`netem`. containerlab checks the published Link schema the first time a lab\n+uses them, because an older release would drop the field and deploy the lab\n+unimpaired. clabernetes programs the delay in 32-bit kernel ticks, so it\n+accepts delays up to `4m`.\n+\n ## Start, stop, and restart\n \n Node lifecycle commands ask the clabernetes controllers for a run state; they\n never touch Deployments or Pods.\n \n@@ -1413,19 +1448,18 @@ Known command differences:\n - Destroy flags `--graceful` and `--keep-mgmt-net` are rejected. `--cleanup`\n   also deletes the lab's persistent claims (saved device state) and removes\n   the local lab directory; a plain destroy keeps the claims.\n - Local Docker commands on the outer host are not authoritative for c9s labs.\n - `inspect interfaces` lists only the lab link interfaces (those `capture`\n-  accepts), not the management or pod interfaces. Host-side `tc` or netem\n-  operations do not have the same local namespace access they have with Docker\n-  labs.\n+  accepts), not the management or pod interfaces.\n - `graph` renders from the topology file only: `--mermaid`, `--dot`, `--drawio`\n   and `--offline` work, the default mode that reads running containers is\n   rejected, and so is `--node-filter`. `--drawio` runs the clab-io-draw\n   container, so it needs Docker or Podman on the outer host.\n - `tools` commands operate on local containers and host networking and are\n-  rejected with an error when the `c9s` runtime is selected.\n+  rejected with an error when the `c9s` runtime is selected, except\n+  [`tools netem`](#link-impairments), which changes the lab's Links.\n - Per-node `runtime: docker` or `runtime: podman` is not the same as selecting\n   the global `c9s` lab runtime.\n - A lab name maps to one canonical `c9s-<lab-name>` namespace in the selected\n   cluster.\n - c9s 0.9 removed `Topology.spec.naming`. A topology with an explicit\ndiff --git a/docs/manual/impairments.md b/docs/manual/impairments.md\nindex 9a38e29..df0268f 100644\n--- a/docs/manual/impairments.md\n+++ b/docs/manual/impairments.md\n@@ -62,10 +62,8 @@ topology:\n | `rate`       | Rate limit in kbit/s, e.g. `10000`                                    |\n | `corruption` | Random packet corruption in percent, e.g. `10`                        |\n \n \n \n-Impairments are supported on the node endpoints of [veth](topo-def-file.md#veth) and [veth-stitch](topo-def-file.md#veth-stitch) links; other link types and `host` or `mgmt-net` endpoints reject them. On veth-stitch links, which brief links of SR-SIM nodes use, containerlab sets them on the stitch, like `tools netem set` does, since impairments on the interfaces of SR-SIM nodes have no effect. On SR-SIM endpoints of extended `veth` links they have no effect either, and containerlab warns about it.\n-\n-> [clabernetes](clabernetes/runtime.md) lab runtime doesn't support declarative impairments yet, so deploying a topology with impairments there fails, as do starting or restarting its nodes.\n+Impairments are supported on the node endpoints of [veth](topo-def-file.md#veth) and [veth-stitch](topo-def-file.md#veth-stitch) links; other link types and `host` or `mgmt-net` endpoints reject them. On veth-stitch links, which brief links of SR-SIM nodes use, containerlab sets them on the stitch, like `tools netem set` does, since impairments on the interfaces of SR-SIM nodes have no effect. On SR-SIM endpoints of extended `veth` links they have no effect either, and containerlab warns about it. With the [clabernetes runtime](clabernetes/runtime.md#link-impairments), the impairments become part of the lab's Links, and `tools netem` changes them there.\n \n Containerlab sets them again when a node is started or restarted, since a node's interfaces lose their impairments when it is stopped, and whenever the lab is deployed again. `tools netem` can still change them while the lab runs, until containerlab sets the topology's impairments again. Removing an impairment from the topology, or setting all of its values to zero, doesn't remove it from a running lab; use `tools netem reset` for that.\ndiff --git a/go.mod b/go.mod\nindex 941: +	ctx context.Context,
942: +	req clablabruntime.ImpairmentRequest,
943: +) error {
944: +	r, err := r.connect(ctx, req.Identity)
945: +	if err != nil {
946: +		return err
947: +	}
948: +
949: +	if err = r.ensureLinkNetemSupport(ctx); err != nil {
950: +		return err
951: +	}
952: +
953: +	locations, err := r.LocateNode(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{
954: +		Name: req.Name, Namespace: req.Namespace, Nodes: []string{req.Node},
955: +		Identity: req.Identity,
956: +	})
957: +	if err != nil {
958: +		return err
959: +	}
960: +	location := locations[0]
961: +
962: +	_, err = r.client.Resource(topologyGVR).Namespace(location.Namespace).
963: +		Get(ctx, req.Name, metav1.GetOptions{})
964: +	switch {
965: +	case err == nil:
966: +		return fmt.Errorf("c9s lab %s/%s is owned by a Topology resource, whose controller "+
967: +			"reverts changes to its links; declare the impairment in the topology and deploy "+
968: +			"again, or deploy the lab with --no-topology-cr", location.Namespace, req.Name)
969: +	case !apierrors.IsNotFound(err):
970: +		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get clabernetes topology %s/%s: %w",
971: +			location.Namespace, req.Name, err)
972: +	}
973: +
974: +	links, err := r.primitiveResourcesForTopology(ctx, linkGVR, req.Name, location.Namespace)
975: +	if err != nil {
976: +		return err
977: +	}
978: +
979: +	link, endpoint, ok := linkEndpoint(links.Items, location.NodeName, req.Interface)
980: +	if !ok {
981: +		return fmt.Errorf("interface %q of node %q is not on a link of c9s lab %s/%s",
982: +			req.Interface, req.Node, location.Namespace, req.Name)
983: +	}
984: +
985: +	// a merge patch with a null netem removes it
986: +	var netem any
987: +	if req.Impairment != nil {
988: +		netem = linkNetem(req.Impairment)

990: +
991: +	patch, err := json.Marshal(map[string]any{
992: +		"spec": map[string]any{endpoint: map[string]any{"netem": netem}},
993: +	})
994: +	if err != nil {
995: +		return err
996: +	}
997: +
998: +	_, err = r.client.Resource(linkGVR).Namespace(location.Namespace).Patch(

declare the impairment in the topology and deploy \"+\n+\t\t\t\"again, or deploy the lab with --no-topology-cr\", location.Namespace, req.Name)\n+\tcase !apierrors.IsNotFound(err):\n+\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"failed to get clabernetes topology %s/%s: %w\",\n+\t\t\tlocation.Namespace, req.Name, err)\n+\t}\n+\n+\tlinks, err := r.primitiveResourcesForTopology(ctx, linkGVR, req.Name, location.Namespace)\n+\tif err != nil {\n+\t\treturn err\n+\t}\n+\n+\tlink, endpoint, ok := linkEndpoint(links.Items, location.NodeName, req.Interface)\n+\tif !ok {\n+\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"interface %q of node %q is not on a link of c9s lab %s/%s\",\n+\t\t\treq.Interface, req.Node, location.Namespace, req.Name)\n+\t}\n+\n+\t// a merge patch with a null netem removes it\n+\tvar netem any\n+\tif req.Impairment != nil {\n+\t\tnetem = linkNetem(req.Impairment)\n+\t}\n+\n+\tpatch, err := json.Marshal(map[string]any{\n+\t\t\"spec\": map[string]any{endpoint: map[string]any{\"netem\": netem}},\n+\t})\n+\tif err != nil {\n+\t\treturn err\n+\t}\n+\n+\t_, err = r.client.Resource(linkGVR).Namespace(location.Namespace).Patch(\n+\t\tctx, link.GetName(), types.MergePatchType, patch, metav1.PatchOptions{},",

The lifecycle.go diff confirms the P2: the netem check is added only in the `!req.NoTopologyCR`-falls-through branch, i.e., only after `if !req.NoTopologyCR { return r.deployTopology(...) }`. So on the default Topology-CR path (deployTopology) and the reconcile path, no netem support check.

Wait — actually re-read the diff hunk:

```
 	if !req.NoTopologyCR {
 		return r.deployTopology(ctx, req, namespace, prepared, primitiveExists)
 	}
 
+	// The Links are written as compiled here, and an older release would drop their netem.
+	if linksDeclareNetem(primitives.links) {
+		if err = r.ensureLinkNetemSupport(ctx); err != nil {
+			return nil, err
+		}
+	}
```

The comment says "The Links are written as compiled here" — i.e., in the no-topology-cr path, containerlab itself writes the Link manifests. In the Topology-CR path, the clabernetes controller compiles the Links, not containerlab. So containerlab cannot prevent the controller from dropping netem — but it can still detect and fail early, which is the point of the check ("an older release would drop the field and deploy the lab unimpaired" per support.go comment and docs). The check is only reachable via `--no-topology-cr`. On the default path, deploying a topology with impairments against an older clabernetes (<0.12) silently deploys unimpaired. Docs at impairments.md say the clabernetes runtime now supports declarative impairments, and runtime.md says "containerlab checks the published Link schema the first time a lab uses them" — implying it's covered generally, but the check only runs in the no-topology-cr deploy path and in SetImpairment. Hmm — "the first time a lab uses them" — tools netem set does check. But deploy via Topology CR does not check before writing the topology. Also note that once deployed, the Topology-owned lab rejects `set` — so the user cannot even discover the missing netem via `tools netem set`; they'd have to use `show`.

Is this actually a silent failure? The clabernetes 0.11 controller compiles Topology→Links with a 0.11 Link schema; when containerlab creates the Topology CR with link netem fields, the controller would... The Topology CRD in 0.11 — does its schema carry the link netem? The Topology schema in 0.11 may or may not have netem on links. If the Topology CRD prunes unknown fields, netem is dropped at Topology admission; the controller then renders Links without netem. Either way the lab deploys without impairments silently. So the P2 gap is real: the guard the PR introduces for the `--no-topology-cr` path does not cover the default path.

But wait — is it intentional? The comment in lifecycle.go says "The Links are written as compiled here" — acknowledging that this check applies where containerlab writes Links itself. In the Topology-CR path, containerlab doesn't write Links. But the check would still be a correct early failure. The docs claim "containerlab checks the published Link schema the first time a lab uses them" — a deploy with impairments on the default path is a use that isn't checked. So it's a correctness gap vs the PR's own stated intent (docs + support.go comment: "An older release prunes the unknown netem field from a Link, so a lab would deploy without its impairments instead of failing"). P2.

Hmm, but one more consideration: in the Topology-CR path, the Topology CRD itself may prune `netem` from topology links (0.11 Topology schema wouldn't know the field). Actually in containerlab the topology definition is stored; compile happens controller-side. Either way, silent.

Also — does `deployTopology`/`reconcileTopology` even have `primitives` available? Yes, `prepared.primitives.links`. And the deploy function receives `prepared`. So the fix: hoist the check above the `if !req.NoTopologyCR` early return in `Deploy`.

167: +
168: +func netemLab(o *Options) (*clabcore.CLab, error) {

171: +			o.Global.Runtime)
172: +	}
173: +
174: +	c, err := clabcore.NewContainerLab(o.ToClabOptions()...)
175: +	if err != nil {
176: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to load topology: %w", err)
177: +	}
178: +
179: +	return c, nil
180: +}
181: +
182: +func netemSetLabRuntime(ctx context.Context, o *Options) error {
183: +	c, err := netemLab(o)
184: +	if err != nil {
185: +		return err
186: +	}
187: +
188: +	err = c.SetLinkImpairment(ctx, clablabruntime.ImpairmentRequest{
189: +		Node:      o.ToolsNetem.ContainerName,
190: +		Interface: o.ToolsNetem.Interface,
191: +		Impairment: &clablabruntime.Impairment{
192: +			Delay:      o.ToolsNetem.Delay,
193: +			Jitter:     o.ToolsNetem.Jitter,
194: +			Loss:       o.ToolsNetem.Loss,
195: +			Rate:       o.ToolsNetem.Rate,
196: +			Corruption: o.ToolsNetem.Corruption,
197: +		},
198: +	})
199: +	if err != nil {
200: +		return err
201: +	}
202: +
203: +	nodes, err := c.LinkImpairments(ctx, []string{o.ToolsNetem.ContainerName})
204: +	if err != nil {
205: +		return err
206: +	}
207: +
208: +	for _, node := range nodes {
209: +		for _, impairment := range node.Impairments {
210: +			if impairment.Interface == o.ToolsNetem.Interface {
211: +				printImpairments([]tableWriter.Row{impairmentTableRow(impairment)})
212: +			}
213: +		}
214: +	}
215: +
216: +	return nil
217: +}
218: +
219: +func netemShowLabRuntime(ctx context.Context, o *Options) error {
220: +	c, err := netemLab(o)
221: +	if err != nil {
222: +		return err
223: +	}
224: +
225: +	var requested []string
226: +	if o.ToolsNetem.ContainerName != "" {
227: +		requested = []string{o.ToolsNetem.ContainerName}
228: +	}
229: +
230: +	nodes, err := c.LinkImpairments(ctx, requested)
231: +	if err != nil {
232: +		return err
233: +	}
234: +
235: +	if o.ToolsNetem.Format == clabconstants.FormatJSON {
236: +		impairments := make(map[string][]clabtypes.ImpairmentData, len(nodes))
237: +		for _, node := range nodes {
238: +			impairments[node.Node] = node.Impairments
239: +		}
240: +
241: +		jsonData, err := json.MarshalIndent(impairments, "", "  ")
242: +		if err != nil {
243: +			return fmt.Errorf("error marshaling JSON: %v", err)
244: +		}
245: +
246: +		fmt.Println(string(jsonData))
247: +
248: +		return nil
249: +	}
250: +
251: +	for _, node := range nodes {
252: +		if len(requested) == 0 {
253: +			fmt.Printf("\n=== Node: %s ===\n", node.Node)
254: +		}
255: +
256: +		rows := make([]tableWriter.Row, 0, len(node.Impairments))
257: +		for _, impairment := range node.Impairments {
258: +			rows = append(rows, impairmentTableRow(impairment))
259: +		}
260: +
261: +		printImpairments(rows)
262: +	}
263: +
264: +	return nil
265: +}
266: +
267: +func netemResetLabRuntime(ctx context.Context, o *Options) error {
268: +	c, err := netemLab(o)
269: +	if err != nil {
270: +		return err
271: +	}
272: +
273: +	err = c.SetLinkImpairment(ctx, clablabruntime.ImpairmentRequest{
274: +		Node:      o.ToolsNetem.ContainerName,
275: +		Interface: o.ToolsNetem.Interface,
276: +	})
277: +	if err != nil {
278: +		return err
279: +	}
280: +
281: +	fmt.Printf("Reset impairments on node %q, interface %q\n",
282: +		o.ToolsNetem.ContainerName, o.ToolsNetem.Interface)
283: +
284: +	return nil
285: +}
286: +
287: +// impairmentTableRow formats an impairment like the table tools netem show prints for local
288: +// labs.
289: +func impairmentTableRow(impairment clabtypes.ImpairmentData) tableWriter.Row {
290: +	return tableWriter.Row{
291: +		impairment.Interface,
292: +		impairment.Delay,
293: +		impairment.Jitter,
294: +		strconv.FormatFloat(impairment.PacketLoss, 'f', 2, 64) + "%",
295: +		strconv.Itoa(impairment.Rate),
296: +		strconv.FormatFloat(impairment.Corruption, 'f', 2, 64) + "%",
297: +	}
298: +}

477: +}

2. **P4** — All-zero `tools netem set` leaves `netem: {}` on the Link and prints nothing. Location: head `labruntime/clabernetes/netem.go` L204-225 (`linkNetem`) + `labruntime/clabernetes/netem.go` L141 (Impairments skip) + `cmd/tools_netem_labruntime.go` L62-68 (print loop). Root cause: `linkNetem` returns empty map for zero impairment; merge patch writes `netem: {}`; `Impairments` skips empty netem so the confirmation table is empty. Suggestion: treat an all-zero impairment as a reset in `netemSetLabRuntime` (send nil), or skip the patch when all values are zero, so behavior matches `reset`.

Hmm, is it P4 or P3? "set with no impairment values" is a degenerate call; the user-visible effect is a silently no-op set that leaves an empty object in the CR. I'll call it P4 (optional improvement), acknowledging low impact.

3. Possibly a P4 on docs: runtime.md says "containerlab checks the published Link schema the first time a lab uses them" — overstated given finding 1. But that's part of finding 1's correction (docs would become accurate once the check is hoisted). I'll fold it into finding 1 rather than a separate finding.

Anything else? Let me reconsider the `validateInputAndRoot` ordering: lab-runtime branch returns nil before root check — correct for c9s (no root needed). But note `validateInputAndRoot` is called where? In set's PersistentPreRun presumably. `netemShowFn` doesn't call validateInputAndRoot? Local show doesn't need root. OK.

Also `netemSetFn` lab-runtime branch happens after the `-n` required check — but before `modprobe sch_netem`, good (c9s doesn't need modprobe).

One more possible issue: `netemLab` requires topo or name — with `-r c9s` and only `--name`, `NewContainerLab` builds from the inventory saved in the lab dir... For c9s, does `--name` path work? The lab directory for c9s labs — does containerlab save the topology/inventory for c9s labs? The docs say "It needs --topo or --name". Presumably the inventory exists. Fine.

Also `Impairments` uses `locations[0].Namespace` for the list — LocateNode returns nodes of one lab; all same namespace. Fine.

Edge: `Impairments` when `req.Nodes` lists a nonexistent node → LocateNode error → propagate. Fine.

Edge: two endpoints of the same link on the same node? c9s links are between distinct nodes presumably. Not an issue.

`SetImpairment` patch: uses `endpoint` field name; if the same interface appears on both endpoints of one link (self-loop)? Not realistic.

Test note: `Impairments` result includes `{Node: "r2"}` with nil Impairments — the `netemShowLabRuntime` prints a header + empty table for r2 in table mode. In JSON mode, `impairments["r2"] = nil` → marshals as `null`. Robot test only checks client. Fine.
