Reasoning
Local behavior with all-zero set: `ReplaceImpairments` replaces the qdisc with a zero netem qdisc (limit 10000) — so local set with all zeros installs a zero-impairment qdisc (netem still present, clab `tc qdisc show` would show `netem` but with no loss/delay... actually qdisc shows "netem" kind with default state). Whereas lab-runtime set with all zeros writes `netem: {}` — clabwire sees an empty netem and presumably doesn't install any qdisc; `show` reports nothing.

The divergence is real but minor and the degenerate call (`set` with no flags) has no meaningful impairment semantics either way. P4 stands.

Now write the final review. Findings:

1. P2 — Netem support check bypassed on the default Topology-CR deploy path.
   Location: head labruntime/clabernetes/lifecycle.go L88-L106.
   Problem: `Deploy` early-returns through `reconcileTopology` (L89-96) and `deployTopology` (L97-99) before the `linksDeclareNetem`/`ensureLinkNetemSupport` guard (L101-106), so only `--no-topology-cr` deploys run it. `SetImpairment` and `checkLabRuntimeLinkImpairments` gate separately.
   Trigger: `deploy -r c9s -t lab.clab.yml` (default path) against clabernetes <0.12 with a topology declaring `netem`.
   Impact: The controller (or Topology CRD pruning) drops the netem and the lab deploys silently unimpaired — exactly the failure mode the PR's own comments (`support.go` requiredClabernetesNetem) and docs (`docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md` "containerlab checks the published Link schema the first time a lab uses them") promise to prevent. Worse, on a Topology-owned lab `SetImpairment` rejects changes, so the user cannot discover or fix it with `tools netem`.
   Correction: hoist the guard above the two early returns in `Deploy` — `prepared.primitives.links` is available on both paths since `prepareDesiredDeployment` (plan.go L27) always compiles primitives — and adjust the comment ("The Links are written as compiled here" applies only to the no-topology-cr branch).

2. P4 — All-zero `tools netem set` on a lab runtime writes `netem: {}` and prints nothing.
   Location: head labruntime/clabernetes/netem.go L204-L225 (`linkNetem`) with cmd/tools_netem_labruntime.go L42-L68.
   Problem: `netemSetLabRuntime` always passes a non-nil `&Impairment{}`; with all-zero values `linkNetem` returns an empty map, which patches `netem: {}` onto the Link. `Impairments` (L141) skips endpoints whose `len(netem) == 0`, so the post-set confirmation table prints nothing, and `show` reports the interface as unimpaired. Local `tools netem set` instead replaces the qdisc with a zero-impairment netem qdisc (`netem/netem.go` ReplaceImpairments), so the two runtimes diverge on the same command.
   Trigger: `tools netem set -r c9s -t lab.clab.yml -n r1 -i eth1` with no impairment flags.
   Impact: Silent no-op with a leftover empty object in the CR; cosmetic inconsistency.
   Correction: treat an all-zero impairment as a reset in `netemSetLabRuntime` (pass `nil`), or skip the patch when all fields are zero.

## Review: `tools netem` support under lab runtimes (clabernetes)

**Head:** `9c4339862aaf88770cd98d951e994c7f5afb87f2` · **Base:** `e7f598179e26c61d406af854da48d39565f4aa7d`

### Summary

The PR adds `tools netem` support for lab runtimes: a `LinkImpairer` capability on `labruntime.Runtime`, a clabernetes implementation that reads/writes `netem` on c9s Link endpoints, an OpenAPI-based schema check for clusters older than clabernetes 0.12, an exception in the lab-runtime command gate for `tools.netem`, tests, docs, and an e2e suite. The wiring is clean and well-tested. One correctness gap remains in where the new support check is executed.

### Severity summary

| Priority | Count | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| P2 | 1 | Netem support check is bypassed on the default Topology-CR deploy path |
| P4 | 1 | All-zero `tools netem set` on a lab runtime leaves `netem: {}` and prints nothing |

### Findings

#### P2 — Netem support check is bypassed on the default Topology-CR deploy path

**Location:** [`labruntime/clabernetes/lifecycle.go` L88-L106](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/9c4339862aaf88770cd98d951e994c7f5afb87f2/labruntime/clabernetes/lifecycle.go#L88-L106) (head)

**Problem:** In `Deploy`, the new guard runs only after two early returns: `existingTopology != nil` returns through `reconcileTopology` (lines 89-96) and `!req.NoTopologyCR` returns through `deployTopology` (lines 97-99), both before the check:

```go
if linksDeclareNetem(primitives.links) {
    if err = r.ensureLinkNetemSupport(ctx); err != nil { ... }
}
```

Neither `deployTopology` ([reconcile.go L404-L497](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/9c4339862aaf88770cd98d951e994c7f5afb87f2/labruntime/clabernetes/reconcile.go#L404-L497)) nor `reconcileTopology` (L534-L593) runs the check. So the guard exists only for `--no-topology-cr` deploys (where containerlab itself writes the compiled Links) and for `SetImpairment`.

**Trigger:** `containerlab -r c9s deploy -t lab.clab.yml` (the default path) with a topology that declares `netem`, against a cluster running clabernetes older than 0.12.

**Impact:** An older controller (or Topology CRD pruning) drops the impairment and the lab deploys silently unimpaired — exactly the failure mode the PR is designed to catch, per its own comments in `support.go` (`requiredClabernetesNetem`: "An older release prunes the unknown netem field from a Link, so a lab would deploy without its impairments instead of failing") and the new docs in `docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md` ("containerlab checks the published Link schema the first time a lab uses them"). It is worse on this path than on the `--no-topology-cr` path: a Topology-owned lab rejects `SetImpairment` by design, so the user cannot even probe the missing support with `tools netem set`; only `show` would reveal it indirectly.

**Correction:** Hoist the guard above the two early returns in `Deploy`. `prepareDesiredDeployment` ([plan.go L27](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/9c4339862aaf88770cd98d951e994c7f5afb87f2/labruntime/clabernetes/plan.go#L27)) always compiles `primitives` on both paths, so `prepared.primitives.links` is available there. Adjust the comment, which currently applies only to the `--no-topology-cr` branch ("The Links are written as compiled here"). A unit test asserting that `Deploy` fails on both paths with a netem-declaring topology and an unsupported cluster would pin the behavior.

#### P4 — All-zero `tools netem set` on a lab runtime leaves `netem: {}` and prints nothing

**Location:** [`labruntime/clabernetes/netem.go` L204-L225](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/9c4339862aaf88770cd98d951e994c7f5afb87f2/labruntime/clabernetes/netem.go#L204-L225) with [`cmd/tools_netem_labruntime.go` L42-L68](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/9c4339862aaf88770cd98d951e994c7f5afb87f2/cmd/tools_netem_labruntime.go#L42-L68) (head)

**Problem:** `netemSetLabRuntime` always passes a non-nil `&Impairment{}` built from the flags. When all flags are zero (the default), `linkNetem` returns an empty map, and the merge patch writes `netem: {}` onto the Link endpoint. `Impairments` skips endpoints whose `netem` is empty (line 141), so the post-set confirmation loop in `netemSetLabRuntime` prints nothing and a subsequent `show` reports the interface as unimpaired. For comparison, local `tools netem set` with all zeros replaces the interface's qdisc with a zero-impairment netem qdisc (`netem/netem.go`, `ReplaceImpairments`), so the same command behaves differently across runtimes.

**Trigger:** `containerlab -r c9s tools netem set -t lab.clab.yml -n r1 -i eth1` with no impairment flags.

**Impact:** A silent no-op that leaves an empty object in the CR; cosmetic inconsistency with the local runtime and with `reset`.

**Correction:** Treat an all-zero impairment as a reset in `netemSetLabRuntime` (pass `nil` for `Impairment`), or skip the patch when all fields are zero. Either keeps `set`, `show`, and `reset` consistent.

### Coverage notes

- This was a source-only review; the snapshot does not permit executing tests, linters, or the formatter, and no CI results were supplied.
- All 22 changed paths from `manifest.json` were reviewed, including the diff hunks for `cmd/root.go`, `cmd/root_test.go`, `cmd/tools_netem.go`, `core/labruntime.go`, `core/labruntime_gaps_test.go`, `labruntime/clabernetes/{clabernetes,lifecycle,support,netem}.go`, all test files, docs, `go.mod`/`go.sum`, and the e2e suite.
- Command gating verified: `checkLabRuntimeCommandSupport` walks parent commands and `break`s on the `tools.netem` path in `labRuntimeSupportedCommands`; other `tools` subcommands (e.g., `tools sshx`) remain rejected, covered by `cmd/root_test.go`.
- Schema check: `schemas/clab.schema.json` is unchanged and already carries `netem` on links (a pre-existing local feature); the new `tests/14-clabernetes/03-link-netem.clab.yml` validates against it, so no schema edit is needed. The c9s Link CRD schema is external (clabernetes v0.12.0, per `go.mod`), and the PR validates it at runtime through the OpenAPI check with a committed fixture and unit tests.
- Unverified by execution: whether clabernetes 0.11 prunes or rejects link-level `netem` on Topology admission; the P2 conclusion (silent unimpaired deploy) holds either way.
- The documented 4 m delay ceiling (32-bit kernel ticks) is not validated client-side in `linkNetem`; it is an external clabernetes/kernel constraint that the docs disclose, and local netem shares the same kernel limit, so it is recorded here rather than raised as a finding.
- The generated `docs/cmd/tools/netem/*.md` pages are unchanged, which is consistent with the unchanged Long help texts of the netem commands.
